#1654. FIFA Slaps Real Madrid, Atletico Madrid With 1-Year Transfer Bans

Home » Home 2 » FIFA Slaps Real Madrid, Atletico Madrid With 1-Year Transfer Bans

The ban will start from the July transfer window this year and finish with the January transfer market in 2017.

Atletico were also fined 900,000 Swiss francs (820,000 euros) and Real 360,000 (330,000 euros).

“The two clubs were found to have violated several provisions concerning the international transfer and first registration of minor players as well as other relevant provisions with regard to the registration and participation of certain players in competitions,” said a FIFA statement.

Barcelona has just ended a one year ban for similar reasons.

Real and Atletico were “issued with a reprimand and given 90 days in which to regularise the situation of all minor players concerned,” FIFA said. They can still sell players during the transfer ban.

FIFA said the alarm was raised over the two clubs by FIFA’s Transfer Matching System and its disciplinary committee completed the inquiry.

Under international football rules, players under 18 cannot be transferred to another country, except in limited circumstances. All transfers need the approval of a special FIFA committee.

“The investigations concerned minor players who were involved and participated in competitions with the clubs over various periods between 2007 and 2014 (Atletico Madrid) and between 2005 and 2014 (Real Madrid),” FIFA said.

The ban follows a similar sanction handed to European champions Barcelona, who were unable to register new players during 2015.

Barca were initially banned in April 2014, but managed to delay the sanction taking affect until the transfer windows in January and the summer 2015 by launching an ultimately unsuccessful appeal to the Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS).

By delaying the ban, Barca managed to sign the likes of Luis Suarez and Ivan Rakitic in the summer of 2014 to propel them to a treble of La Liga, Champions League and Copa del Rey.

The news is just the latest institutional embarassment for Real Madrid just over a week after they appointed French legend Zinedine Zidane.

Madrid have sacked two Champions League winning coaches in Carlo Ancelotti and Rafael Benitez in the past seven months, as well as being thrown out of the Copa del Rey for fielding an ineligible player.

The sanction could also be bad news for the likes of Paris Saint-Germain and Manchester United, who had targeted Madrid stars Cristiano Ronaldo and Gareth Bale with Real highly unlikely to dispose of their best players without the chance to sign suitable replacements.

La Liga leaders Atletico Madrid’s usually hectic transfer policy will also be put on hold. However, Diego Simeone’s men look better placed to cope with the ban having invested heavily in young talent over the past year.

Neither Real no Atletico made an immediate comment on whether they would appeal.

#1650. Ramos upset by substitution: The clarification and why Cisse came on over Camarda

Goncalo Ramos got his name on the scoresheet in AC Milan’s rout of Frosinone, but he was forced off in the second half.

As Sky (via Calciomercato.com) report, everything seemed great when Milan were dominating Frosinone at San Siro and scoring nearly every time they went forward. However, during the second half, a minor alarm sounded.

Ruben Amorim was forced to replace his Ramos in the 50th minute. The Portuguese striker – who had scored in the first half – was hastily removed from the pitch by the head coach shortly after Ardon Jashari’s goal to make it 3-1.

The reason? The change was made due to a minor muscle problem that the player reported to the bench, even though Ramos himself did not seem happy about the substitution at the time of the change.

The former PSG man informed the bench that he had a small calf problem and – to avoid worsening the issue – Amorim immediately opted for a substitution. Alphadjo Cisse was sent on in his place, and he scored the fourth goal just a few minutes later.

When he was taken off, Ramos showed a grimace of disapproval towards his bench, miming the ‘wait’ gesture. He then complained that he would have liked to try to stay on the pitch, but some post-match comments cleared things up.

When asked if his calf is ok, he told DAZN: “Yes, yes, everything’s fine, everything’s fine.” Rabiot later revealed the background to the substitution to Sky, admitting that he played a hand in convincing the coach.

“Gonçalo is the first player to do a lot. Today I saw he had a bit of pain in his thigh. I know he’s a very important player for us, and we have a lot of matches. I even asked the coach to let him rest a bit,” the Frenchman said.

Speaking to DAZN after the final whistle, Amorim was asked why he felt it was right for Cisse to come on rather than Francesco Camarda, the only other natural centre-forward in the squad

“We didn’t spend many minutes near the penalty area; he was behind. Today we were 40 metres from the goal, and Cisse was perfect for that. That’s why I didn’t bring on Camarda for Ramos: I needed someone who could run in behind.”

#1649. Celtic 4 St Mirren 1: Oxlade-Chamberlain rolls back the years as champions put Buddies to the sword

By JOHN MCGARRY, SCOTTISH CHIEF SPORTS FEATURE WRITER

Published: 12:32 EST, 21 November 2026 | Updated: 12:48 EST, 21 November 2026

What Martin O’Neill wouldn’t give to see more of this until the point where the cavalry appears on top of the hill in January.

Celtic wins with bells and whistles attached have been as rare as hen’s teeth since this campaign began.

That the supporters witnessed one in trying circumstances felt significant given the arduous schedule which awaits in the coming six weeks.

Despite having no option but to piece together a midfield, O’Neill watched his side create a slew of opportunities. They took four with as many different scorers and might well have had more.

A display brimming with enterprise and imagination boded well for what lies ahead. For the first time since September, Celtic have chalked up three straight wins. Ahead of the trip to face Torreense in Portugal on Thursday, it appears that a bit of wind is back in the sails.

This was as comprehensive a win as the scoreline suggests. The champions were never in danger from the moment Alex Oxlade-Chamberlain edged them in front just after the half hour mark.

Alex Oxlade-Chamberlain celebrates Celtic's first goal against St Mirren

In danger of becoming something of a forgotten man, the former England man rolled back the years here with a display which reminded you why he once wore the shirts of Liverpool and Arsenal. On this evidence, he still has a contribution to make at Parkhead.

The outcome was more or less settled by the interval. Camilo Duran continued his outstanding first season in Glasgow’s East End with another assured finish.

Luke McCowan, a man who’s not exactly had his critics to seek in recent times, netted the third before the break, his goal a just reward for a tidy afternoon’s work.

On a day when O’Neill would have had concerns about his midfield, Callum McGregor also netted with a crisp strike from the edge of the box.

St Mirren’s consolation, coming from Killian Phillips’ penalty, was too little too late.

On Friday, Buddies boss Craig McLeish had made some salient points about the self-interest which is holding back Scottish football.

It’s hard not to like McLeish’s attitude and the style of football his side are playing. But they are continuing to lose goals far too easily. They could find themselves getting dragged into trouble if they don’t quickly address it.

Celtic's Camilo Duran celebrates after scoring their second goal in the 4-1 win

On Friday, O’Neill had rejected the suggestion that Haissem Hassan had been omitted from the squad which faced Kilmarnock because he needed a kick up the backside. Yet, curiously, there was no sign of the Egyptian again here.

With Benjamin Nygren and Mika Baur injured, O’Neill hoped that a combination of McGregor, McCowan and Oxlade-Chamberlain would have enough.

Kasper Hogh’s chances of ending a run of 16 games without a goal weren’t helped by him starting on the bench. He didn’t leave it.

With just one win in nine coming into this, Craig McLeish’s side were short on points yet they were not short on confidence.

Although they played some stuff which was very easy on the eye, an inability to keep the ball out of the net cost them dear again.

McCowan had an early shot blocked before Colby Donovan had a weak effort saved. McCowan also hesitated to take a first-time strike with Louis Jackson doing enough to protect Jacob Chapman’s goal.

Celtic actually had the ball in the net twice before they made it count. Duran planted a header and a shot in the visitors’ net only to discover that the offside flag had been raised.

Jota sparked a sweeping move which saw Yang Hyun-jun tee up McCowan. Paul Nsio became the latest Saints player to frustrate the Celtic midfielder with a block.

Saints were aggrieved that Yang won a free-kick by going to ground too easily just before the opener. They may have had a point. That didn’t excuse the defending which followed.

Cameron Carter-Vickers rolled the ball in Yang’s direction. The winger burst away from Declan John and assessed his options.

His cut-back for the unmarked Oxlade-Chamberlain was inch-perfect. The former England midfielder swept home his first goal since netting against the same opponent in April.

Saints might well have levelled immediately. Ismeal Kabia wriggled away from Donovan and picked out Eseosa Sule. Liam Scales did well to prevent the forward netting from seven yards.

Celtic then cut through Saints with embarrassing ease. A straight pass sent Yang clear on goal. He should have gone for glory, but instead tried to square the ball to allow Duran a tap-in. Alex Gogic had other ideas and knocked the ball away for a corner.

Celtic midfielder Luke McCowan and St Mirren's Paul Nsio battle for the ball

McLeish’s hopes of making it to the break still in the contest unravelled in the final five minutes of the first period.

Kieran Tierney’s decision to swap flanks paid dividends with a brilliant in-swinging cross. Duran ghosted onto it and cushioned the ball beyond Chapman with his left foot to claim his 14th goal of his debut season.

Jota might well have made it three-nil seconds later and he fired Oxlade-Chamberlain’s lay-off straight at the keeper.

There was no hope for Chapman as Celtic all but wrapped up the win three minutes before the interval.

Tierney was again the provider, his energy taking him to the line and allowing him to cross. McCowan calmly stroked home his second goal of the season.

Saints kept going seeking a goal which might have made it interesting. Kabia’s strike forced Sam Johnstone into a smart stop down to his right.

Yang ought to have killed the contest but blazed over while leaning back. Skipper McGregor showed him how to do it as he buried a right foot shot low in the bottom left-hand corner from the edge of the box after a defender had taken the ball off Duran’s toe.

Saints did get on the board thanks to Phillips’ penalty conversion, the award coming after Johnstone clattered Calvin Ramsay as he punched clear.

O’Neill was still able to send on Shim Mheaka and James Forrest with Austin Trusty returning to warm applause. Joel van den Berg had already been introduced for his debut along with Callum Osmand. The Dutch teenager showed up well.

#1648. Sampdoria swept aside by rampant Napoli – are the Partenopei on course for their first Scudetto in 26 years?

Home » Home 2 » Sampdoria swept aside by rampant Napoli – are the Partenopei on course for their first Scudetto in 26 years?

Dries Mertens celebrating with his team-mates on the touchline after his decisive goal in the 4-2 victory at Sampdoria is typical of the spirit and togetherness that has seen Napoli storm to the top of the Serie A title. It was in dedication to Chelsea loanee Nathaniel Chabolah who recently lost his mother a a nice touch to show that there is much more to life than football, even though they have put themselves in a wonderful position to end Juventusa dominance and end a 26-year wait for the Scudetto.

Five straight wins have put Maurizio Sarria s team two points clear at the top, with the former Empoli manager breathing a new lease of life throughout a team that have always looked capable of competing for the title, yet ultimately fallen short when the pressure to deliver grew. He has transformed the entire dynamics of how Napoli play, with clinical attacking movement combined with a rock-solid defence within a 4-3-3 system that is getting the very best from the players at his disposal. This seasona s statistics proved that point; Napoli are far and away the highest scorers in Serie A this season, while only Inter Milan and Juventus have a better defensive record. Just one defeat in the twenty league games since the opening day loss at Sassuolo is another illustration of just how good Napoli have been this season, with the crushing 4-0 win at AC Milan in early October a sign of what the Partenopei are truly capable of.

Juventus were always likely to be favourites for the Scudetto on Coral and any other football odds site as their dominance of Italian football threatens to extend into its fifth season, so it is perhaps refreshing from a purista s perspective that Napoli have emerged as real contenders to challenge the Bianconeri. Massimo Allegria s side have stormed up the table in ominous fashion following a surprisingly slow start to the season, with eleven straight victories serving a serious warning to Napoli that they will make them fight all the way for the 2015/2016 Serie A title. It remains to be seen how Sarri and his team handle the pressure of having Juventus breathing down their necks, but the fact they have scored twelve goals in their last three games would indicate that

Some may have been surprised by Gonzalo Higuaina s decision to swap Real Madrid for Naples in the summer of 2013, but the 28-year-old has become one of the most feared strikers in Italy. The Argentine international has formed a wonderful strikeforce at the front of a three-man attack, with Jose Callejon and Lorenzo Insigne adding searing pace and skill on either side of a frontman who has made a career from being a true predator inside the box.

Twenty-one games in as many Serie A games this season puts him amongst the most in-form strikers in world football, with his clinical finish which opened the scoring against Sampdoria proving just how good he has been in front of goal. It is the sort of purple patch that any striker worth their salt would dream to be in; Coral have unsurprisingly backed Higuain as favourite to score in their next game against Sarria s former employers Empoli who have kept just one clean sheet from their last five league fixtures. Napoli will need Higuain to carry his rich vein of form throughout the rest of the season if they are to have any chance of maintaining their wonderful pace and sprint clear of the chasing pack.

Napoli have won many admirers across Europe for the quality of football they have played this season, but it remains to be seen if they have the mentality to pass the acid test and keep the momentum going between now and the end of the season. Recent history would suggest that their chances are not great; the Partenopei, then managed by Walter Mazzarri, put themselves in a wonderful position in 2012/2013, only to finish runners-up behind Juventus as the odd slip at the wrong times proved costly in their pursuit of Juventus. A number of third-placed finishes would also suggest that Napoli have lacked the mentality and guile to end their long wait for a Scudetto, but there is real excitement in Naples that the current crop of players have what it takes to stop the Old Lady from making it five titles in a row.

#1647. EPL Prepares for Most Exciting Title Race in Years

Home » Home 2 » EPL Prepares for Most Exciting Title Race in Years

Now that all of the top four English Premier League teams have had a chance to play each other, we find ourselves looking at one of the most wide open title races in recent memory. As of this writing, the league leaders are only separated by a mere six points. With the exception of Manchester City, we could very well see a new face hoisting the Premier League trophy at the end of the season.

For much of the year, it looked like Arsenal would be in the running for its first league title in more than a decade. With the Gunners’ recent victory against Leicester City, they are very much back in the conversation. Danny Welbeck returned to the pitch for the first time this season and made an immediate impact for Arsene Wenger’s squad, scoring the last-minute, game-winning goal to propel the team to within two points of the top spot. Given that even more key players are set to return to action for Arsenal in the coming months, this is easily the best shot they have had of winning a championship since their undefeated 2003-04 season.

Another surprise team that certainly deserves its own mention is Tottenham Hotspur. Following the club’s controversial defeat of Manchester City, the Spurs sit in second place, a mere two points behind Leicester City and ahead of Arsenal on goal differential. Tottenham have yet to win a title in the Premier League era and they have not won an English championship since 1961. The team has done a superb job of backing up star striker Harry Kane with a glut of promising young players, and their goal tally only helps to reinforce the wisdom behind the strategy of manager Mauricio Pochettino.

Meanwhile, Manchester City is still hoping to snag its third title as something of a swan song for exiting manager Manuel Pellegrini. It was recently announced that the club had hired Pep Guardiola . from Bayern Munich to take charge of the team beginning with next season. Thus, Pellegrini has been forced to endure the rest of the campaign as a dead man walking. Despite the impending exit of Pellegrini, City are still in the race for the Premier League title in addition to both the F.A. Cup and Champions League. Theoretically, the club could pull off a treble, if it can manage a solid string of performances during the final half of the season.

At the beginning of the season, it was expected that the usual suspects would once again dominate the league. Many predicted the reigning champs at Chelsea to repeat their success. However, a shocking season has seen the team part ways with controversial manager Jose Mourinho and struggle to remain in the top half of the tables with hopes of a Champions League spot dashed long ago.

For the first time in years, there’s a chance to see a completely new team win the league. No matter which club you support, there’s no denying that this has made for one of the most thrilling contests in recent memory. In a league where money talks, small fish like Leicester City are surprising everyone, and we can only hope that this means a new era of parity for the Premier League.

#1644. The Rock of London: Looking back at John Terry’s Chelsea FC career

Home » Home 2 » The Rock of London: Looking back at John Terry’s Chelsea FC career

At the start of this season, John Terry leaving Chelsea was the last thing on anyone’s mind. All was rosy at Stamford Bridge, the home of the newly crowed English champions. In over 21 years at the club, there was no indication that Terry would not retire a Chelsea man.

The Blues’ skipper’s announcement in January 2016, then, came as a shock to the Chelsea faithful, bringing notice to the seemingly premature — even if inevitable — fall of the curtain on a legendary career.

After making his debut in the League Cup against Aston Villa late in 1998, John Terry made sporadic appearances under Gianluca Vialli, before joining Nottingham Forest on a short loan spell. He broke into the first team in 2000-01, when manager Claudio Ranieri handed him 22 Premier League appearances during a season that the 20-year-old would finish as the club’s Player of the Year.

It would be the first of several achievements to come.

Terry’s importance to the team grew as Ranieri relied on his partnership with then-captain Marcel Desailly to mastermind Chelsea’s progression from a fashionable mid-table club to a Champions League team that meant business. They received a major shot in the arm when Russian billionaire Roman Abramovich bought the club in 2003. It was also a significant year in Terry’s international career as he made his England debut against Serbia and Montenegro in June.

The season that followed saw Chelsea finish above perennial winners Manchester United for the first time in Premier League history, and defeat Premiership invincibles Arsenal en route to the club’s first Champions League semifinal. Terry ended the season making a first of four appearances in the PFA Team of the Year, and went to Portugal for the European Championships having displaced Sol Campbell as England’s first choice centre-back.

In the summer of 2004, Chelsea brought in Jose Mourinho, who was fresh from winning a treble with the unfancied FC Porto and raring to take on bigger challenges. The 23-year-old Terry was named captain as Chelsea embarked on the most successful period in the club’s history. In the three seasons that followed, Chelsea won 2 league cups, 2 Premier League titles and the FA Cup — success built on a core of John Terry, Frank Lampard, Petr Cech and Didier Drogba, Chelsea’s ‘old guard’.

This was also a period when Terry picked up several individual accolades. He was named PFA Player of the Year in 2005, the first defender to win the award since Paul McGrath in 1993. He would make a first of five consecutive appearances in the FIFPro World XI in 2005, as well as a first of four appearances in the UEFA Team of the Year.

He was also voted Chelsea’s Player of the Year for the second time in his career in 2006. Steve McClaren, hired as England manager after an underwhelming 2006 World Cup, named the Chelsea skipper as England captain.

Terry was now, beyond argument, one of football’s best.

However, more testing times were to come.

September 2007 saw the departure of Mourinho after a falling out with the club board. The season itself promised much but left a Chelsea squad dejected on three occasions as they saw the League Cup, the Premier League and the Champions League trophies go elsewhere.

For the European Cup in particular, Terry was left with no one but himself to blame as he slipped for the crucial penalty, a moment he has said will haunt him forever. Chelsea and Terry experienced further European heartbreak the following season as Tom Henning Ovrebo had a refereeing performance to forget at Stamford Bridge, handing Barcelona a berth in the final and eventually the trophy.

In early 2010, when he was revealed as the English footballer who had an affair with Vanessa Perroncel, Wayne Bridge’s ex-girlfriend — a horrendous personal error that cost him his status as England captain — it made him the perennial recipient of passionate booing across English grounds. After the revelation, Chelsea travelled to Burnley. Amidst a frosty reception, he scored a late winner to put Carlo Ancelotti’s side back on track in the title race, one they would go on to win in some style. All of this typified John Terry — imperfect, but unshakeable.

Terry had built an unflappable reputation as a top class defender, leader and hard man. He said about himself, “I still say if the ball is there to be won I will go for it, whether with my head or whatever, and if it means us scoring or stopping a goal, I won’t think twice.”

The period that followed, however, was not good for Chelsea or their captain. The team finished the 2010-11 season trophyless, and Carlo Ancelotti paid for it with his job. This was the first of two times in Terry’s career where he and his club would have an extremely underwhelming season following a dominant one, and it also marked the first attempt to phase him out of the first team.

New manager Andre Villas-Boas attempted to introduce a high defensive line that left Terry exposed on a number of occasions, and saw the young Portuguese manager fall back on quicker defenders to implement his system. He was also determined to make lesser use of Frank Lampard and displace Didier Drogba with Fernando Torres. These were unpopular moves that led to poor results and eventually his sacking. Terry was not helped by another personal abberation, mouthing racial profanity at Anton Ferdinand of QPR, an act that saw him land a lengthy ban and damage his position in the England squad almost beyond repair.

Interim manager Roberto Di Matteo reinstated the old guard, and was rewarded with the ultimate prize — the first Champions League in Chelsea’s history.

Terry retired from international football following EURO 2012, leaving him to focus on his club career. However, further rotation was to follow during the reign of Rafael Benitez, who played Terry only in games of lesser importance. This was something he could do with relative impunity owing to the fact that his stock could not have fallen any further among Chelsea fans.

The writing was seemingly on the wall, however. Unsavoury incidents were fresher in the memory than individual accolades, the skipper was out of favour for two seasons running, and was well over 30 years of age. Was John Terry done?

Mourinho did not share the views of Benitez and Villas-Boas. Where they saw a slowing, easily-exposed has-been, he saw an experienced warrior with an excellent reading of the game who could form a title-winning partnership with the quicker Gary Cahill.

Terry grabbed the opportunity he was handed with gusto, performing with excellence in Mourinho’s lower defensive block. The English pair formed the core of a defence that would go on to win the club’s fourth Premier League title in 2015, leading the table from the opening day to the end. It was a landmark achievement for Terry in particular as he played every minute of a league campaign for the first time in his career, aged 34.

Once again they tried to put him down. Once again he fed off it and rose tall.

Chelsea did not start the defence of their title well at all, gathering just 4 points from the first 4 matches. Mourinho, who asked Terry to take the club on his shoulders in 2004 and stood by him for two seasons in his second stint, hauled off his skipper at half-time at the Etihad in the second game of the season, and began to rotate him out of the team, giving an increasing number of starts to the young Kurt Zouma.

The season did not take much of a turn for the better even under interim manager Guus Hiddink, particularly in a defensive sense as the Blues continued to let in goals during a meek climb to the top half of the table, with or without Terry in the side.

A sending off at the Stadium of Light following an injury layoff is not the kind of ending that the fans desired for their beloved captain, who has emerged from the dugout 703 times in Chelsea colours and has been the face of the club through the most successful period in their history.

Offered a new deal by the club last week, the skipper responded, “The contract extension the club has offered me is a different role and I hope everyone will understand I want to take the time to consider it carefully before making a decision.” While fans will hope — for reasons emotional as well as those to do with football — that Terry stays on, the chances look slim.

Should the captain leave the ship, the Blues supporters’ emotions are best summed up by a certain banner that embellishes the Shed End: Captain, Leader, Legend.

#1642. Giving Youri Tielemans a £35m release clause looks like an error... Aston Villa toiling to a draw with Sunderland was more proof Unai Emery could do with a midfield controller in January, writes TOM COLLOMOSSE

Published: 12:22 EST, 21 November 2026 | Updated: 14:14 EST, 21 November 2026

Whoever put that £35million release clause in Youri Tielemans’ contract has a heck of a lot to think about these days.

The Belgian midfielder left Aston Villa to join Manchester United last summer and though these are early days in his Old Trafford career, the move does not seem to be working out for anyone.

Unai Emery was distraught to lose Tielemans and against Sunderland, you could see why. Emery signed two central midfielders, Leon Goretzka and Joao Gomes, and has given more minutes to Ross Barkley.

None of the three gives him what Tielemans did and Villa may decide to move for another central player in January. Anything for a bit of cleverness in that part of the pitch.

Tielemans has struggled at United and it will be interesting to see what Mauricio Pochettino makes of him. He is no elite athlete and United supporters and pundits have criticised him because of it but he gave Emery what he craves above all else – control. Neither Gomes nor Goretzka has Tielemans’ passing range and Barkley looks more effective higher up the pitch.

With Sunderland sitting deep here, Villa desperately needed a player who could read the game and create angles like Tielemans. Without him, their passing was slow and predictable, against a Sunderland side without key men Dominic Ballard, Granit Xhaka and Brian Brobbey.

Sunderland's Nordi Mukiele stretches for the ball but nobody could find the breakthrough

Regis Le Bris saw his side pick up another point to follow their win over Chelsea before the international break - Sunderland now sit 18th

Their only chance in the first half here fell to Emi Buendia, who won the ball high then failed to chip the back-pedalling Robin Roefs. In the second half, Ian Maatsen and substitute Ibrahim Mbaye shot far too close to the Sunderland goalkeeper, who tipped over another effort from Barkley.

Villa have still not lost in the league since they were beaten here by Nottingham Forest in September but teams aiming for the Champions League should put away Sunderland at home. And after 150 Premier League games at the helm, nobody will know that better than Emery.

Buendia reached Aston Villa immortality last May when he scored in the Europa League final and now he has his own banner.

‘It’s Buendia, with a beauty, on the banks of the Bosphorus’ read the slogan in the Holte End.

They will never forget that 3-0 win over Freiburg here but it is alarming just how quickly the team has split apart since then. Six months have passed since Istanbul but only two of the starting XI from that night – Buendia and Torres – were in Unai Emery’s line-up here.

Emi Buendia is now the subject of a banner from Villa fans for his Europa League final heroics

Youri Tielemans scored a stunner in the Europa League final but is now at Man United

True, Matty Cash and Victor Lindelof were injured, while John McGinn was left on the bench, with one eye on Tuesday’s return to Istanbul to face Galatasaray in the Champions League. Boubacar Kamara missed the final through injury.

Still these are huge changes. For most of Emery’s first four years at Villa, every player knew his role and understood the kind of team they were. Now Villa find themselves learning on the job in a three-sided ground, due to the improvement work that leaves the North Stand empty.

Emery knows it too. ‘We have brought a significant number of new players to the squad, many of whom are still adapting to the demands of competing at the level we have worked so hard to establish ourselves at.

ASTON VILLA (4-2-3-1): Suzuki 6; Wan-Bissaka 6, Harwood-Bellis 6, Torres 7, Maatsen 6; Kamara 6, Goretzka 5 (Barkley 73, 6); Alysson 6, Buendia 6 (McGinn 60, 7), Manzambi 5 (Mbaye 60, 6); Jackson 6 (Madjo 73, 6).

SUNDERLAND (4-2-3-1): Roefs 7; Meunier 7, Mukiele 7, O’Nien 7, Reinildo 7; Ahoka 8, Sadiki 7; Hume 6, Le Fee 7, Talbi 7; Isidor 7 (Angulo 77, 6).

'It takes time, patience, hard work and belief.

‘That is why, now more than ever, we must stick together, trust the direction we are heading in and continue to get behind our players and staff. Results are hugely important but so is recognising the hard work and development that will help us keep moving forward.’

These days clubs like Sunderland cannot afford to wait for young talents to prove themselves in other European leagues.

A decade ago, clubs in the middle of the Premier League could sign players like that for relatively small sums. Now everyone in Europe knows how rich top flight clubs in England are and adjust their prices accordingly.

That is why Sunderland paid nearly £10million for Jules Ahoka even though he had barely played a senior game for Royal Antwerp.

On this evidence, the Black Cats have spent wisely yet again. Ahoka is quick, athletic and strong – exactly what is required in English football today – and his technique is tidy too. If he stays healthy, a bright future awaits.

#1641. Man United captain Bruno Fernandes drops Sporting Lisbon return hint as Portuguese discusses contract situation

By Matt Law | 24 Nov 2026 20:03, Last updated: 24 Nov 2026 20:04

Manchester United captain Bruno Fernandes has said that his future is currently "not important".

Fernandes, 32, only has a contract with the Red Devils until the end of the campaign, but the club do have the option to extend it for a further 12 months.

The Portugal international has reportedly rejected Man United's latest offer, allegedly wanting a longer deal with higher wages given his contribution during a tough period.

There is currently speculation surrounding his future at Old Trafford, but Fernandes has insisted that his main focus for the moment is on helping Man United to turn their campaign around.

"For us to start winning games and then we can talk about contract," Fernandes told reporters ahead of Wednesday's Champions League clash with Sporting Lisbon, when asked what would need to happen for him to sign a new deal.

"It’s not important now. It’s my future, I haven’t got much left in my contract, but we will have time to speak about that. The conversations stopped when we thought now was not the moment."

Fernandes also refused to "close the door" on returning to Sporting before the end of his career.

"I will never close the door to [returning to] Sporting. It will always be a club with a special place in my heart," the Man United captain added.

The Portuguese represented Sporting between 2017 and 2020 ahead of a move to Man United, scoring 63 goals and registering 50 assists in 137 appearances for the club.

Since arriving at Man United, Fernandes has a record of 113 goals and 111 assists in 342 appearances for the English team in all competitions.

Fernandes is again expected to be in the starting side when the Red Devils tackle Sporting in the league stage of the Champions League on Wednesday night.

The playmaker has six goals and three assists in 15 appearances in all competitions this season.

Meanwhile, Fernandes has a record of nine goals and 12 assists in 29 career appearances in the Champions League during his time at Sporting and Man United.

#1640. Floyd Samba’s Man City debut double has father Chris dancing

There was very much a Samba beat to this Manchester City victory – and it almost had a famous father in the crowd up dancing.

This was a night when Brazilian Allan Elias scored his first goal on an enterprising first appearance for City.

But it was another debutant who stole the show as the Carabao Cup holders sailed past Norwich City to set up a fourth-round meeting with Brighton.

Floyd Samba scored two fine goals and had a hand in another on a dream debut that had his beaming dad up off his seat and thrusting his arms in the air as if ready to party.

If the Samba surname feels familiar, that is because Floyd’s father Christopher played more than 200 games for Blackburn Rovers, Queens Park Rangers and Aston Villa.

In fact, it was very much a family affair as Floyd’s brothers Tyrone and Emerson, who are also in City’s academy and hoping one day to tread a similar path, joined in the jubilant celebrations alongside their mother, a visibly emotional Theresa.

This particular evening belonged to Floyd, though. Deployed as a lone striker by Enzo Maresca, you would not have known he ordinarily plays as a midfielder such was the confidence and composure the 17-year-old oozed.

Norwich could not live with him or City for that matter as Maresca’s impressive start as manager since replacing Pep Guardiola continued apace.

This must have been an incredibly satisfying moment for Samba Sr. He came through incredible hardship – at one stage as a teenager he was rough-sleeping – to forge an impressive career totalling more than 450 games for club and country.

So to be in a position to now have three sons in City’s academy and one produce a debut like this will fill him with enormous pride. Floyd was later seen enjoying a warm embrace with his dad in the crowd, moments after being congratulated by Tyrone, a year his senior, and 12-year-old Emerson, who plays for City’s Under-13s.

“I knew there would be an opportunity to get some minutes for the first time with the first team – to get a debut like that is mind blowing,” Samba said. “I couldn’t believe it myself, but that’s just the beginning, I’ve got a big career ahead of me. It was a great debut.”

Floyd caught the eye with a fine free-kick in City’s 2-1 FA Youth Cup final victory over Manchester United last season and now he has goals for the senior side to his name. Pretty stunning they were, too.

The first was a superbly steered header past two Norwich bodies on the line from Allan’s cross and the second a lovely, nonchalantly curled finish low into the far corner.

What a moment for Floyd Samba! 😍A goal on his Man City debut for the 17-year-old, son of former Blackburn defender Chris 🩵 pic.twitter.com/VCVfX9HCNn

Chris Samba has deliberately kept a low profile, keen to let his sons get on with their own careers free of distractions, but there was no chance he was going to be able to suppress his emotions in that instant. And nor should he. It was some moment for the boy and his family.

As impressed as Maresca was by the goals, it will have been other elements of Samba’s game that also caught the eye. He did extremely well to hold off the attentions of Norwich’s centre-backs when receiving a pass from Ayyoub Bouaddi and then returning the ball to the Moroccan who released Rayan Cherki through to score City’s second. His movement was also sharp, at one point taking a difficult pass sweetly in an adjusted strike, only for Norwich’s Bruno Alves to come across to make a timely intervention before Samba could get his shot off.

"Was there any doubt?"Ayyoub Bouaddi with his first assist for Man City as he sets up Rayan Cherki to make it 2-0 🔵 pic.twitter.com/0gfxp5GDXy

“It was satisfying not just for the two goals but for the entire performance,” Maresca said. “He didn’t play many games as a nine but he was good. He’s young, full of energy, strong, he can finish.”

Allan, a £34m summer signing from Palmeiras, will have been just as pleased with his contribution. Maresca’s fluid formation initially resembled a 3-1-5-1 with Allan effectively operating as a right wing-back but he stuck doggedly to the task before eventually getting the moment to showcase his quality, first with his cross for Samba and later with a neat solo run and finish.

Driving inside Sam Field and then cutting back inside the Norwich man before curling an inch perfect finish into the bottom corner – all of it done with his left foot – it was quite the introduction.

Allan on his debut! 🇧🇷Magic from the Brazilian to make it 3-0 to Man City 💥 pic.twitter.com/nw6lNqh1yL

Hugo Viana, City’s director of football, has said supporters will need to be patient with Allan and that it may take the 22-year-old time to adjust to English football but this first outing will do his confidence plenty of good.

“It was important for him to play 90 minutes and to see a little bit the English competition that is a bit different from South America so overall was good,” Maresca said.

Cherki was the only survivor from the team that started Sunday’s victory over Manchester United but it all felt pretty seamless from City. Bouaddi, the £85m signing from Lille, was poised and graceful in midfield alongside the impressive Mateo Kovacic and Geronimo Rulli could not have asked for a much quieter debut in goal.

FLOYD SAMBA again!! 🌟The 17-year-old curls one in to score his second on his Man City debut with his dad Christopher watching on in the stands 👏 pic.twitter.com/fJ5mfEWBx1

Nico O’Reilly looked like he had barely broken a sweat despite Norwich’s players routinely being unable to keep up with him. Norwich themselves made nine changes but the gulf in class was enormous and testament to City’s strength in depth.

The game also gave Maresca the opportunity to give run outs to two more academy graduates who played in that Youth Cup final triumph, Kaden Braithwaite and Ryan McAidoo and the latter got his own name on the scoresheet to make it 5-0.

All told there were seven City academy graduates on the pitch, two of them playing for Norwich. This was certainly a night to remember for the club’s youth production line.

With the dominant performance, Man City have earned themselves the privilege of hosting Brighton in the next round, who will no doubt prove a much stiffer challenge than Norwich. They become the sixth all-Premier League tie in the next round, with only Fleetwood, Bradford and Peterborough remaining from outside the top flight:

Erling Haaland left out of the squad, watching from the stands, would have enjoyed that performance from Floyd Samba. Here is his second goal for you to enjoy on his debut night:

FLOYD SAMBA again!! 🌟The 17-year-old curls one in to score his second on his Man City debut with his dad Christopher watching on in the stands 👏 pic.twitter.com/fJ5mfEWBx1

Five unanswered goals and a home-grown hero emerges for Manchester City!

Great through ball from O’Reilly, which Lewis lets run past him for the dummy. McAidoo runs on to it on the right of the box and first-time fires it low into the far corner.

It has been a perfect night for Manchester City’s academy.

Well we look like we’re heading for a matching scoreline to the previous edition of the fixture. That pesky shot on target is still eluding Norwich, whereas Samba is still out there looking for his hat-trick.

Two minutes of time to be added – who will get there first?

O’Reilly sends a high, looping ball to the back post from the left side, where McAidoo rushes to meet it but can’t get over it under pressure.

Final change for Norwich, as Kvistgaarden who has not had much service tonight, comes off for Schwartau.

Bouaddi sends a looping ball across the field to McAidoo, which he picks up on the edge of the box, but he is unable to get the ball under control to take his shot and it is cleared away as far as another City shirt.

The corner comes in to the centre of the box but is headed out by a City shirt.

It’s all slightly too little too late for Norwich.

They get another corner as Musaba tries to send a cross into the box from the right and it is blocked out.

A free-kick for Norwich now as O’Reilly commits the foul 35 yards out. It goes in towards McConville at the back post, but Ait-Nouri heads it out for a Norwich corner.

Mo Touré strays just offside on the edge of the box, as Musaba sends a lovely little ball over to find him on the turn and the forward slots it past Rulli. Celebrations don’t quite begin before the flag goes up but that is a shame for the visitors.

Norwich have managed to get more of a grip in this half, despite conceding two more goals, but they are still without a shot on goal as we approach the final 15 minutes.

Man City take off scorer of their third goal Allan to bring on Braithwaite.

Norwich replace Ben Slimane and Bruno Alves with Touré and McConville.

Samba again at the heart of the action, laying off the ball to McAidoo on the right for the winger to run into the box. His shot towards the far post is saved low by Grimshaw who spills it almost into the path of Lewis, but Norwich survive.

Lewis makes a run down the right-hand side and crosses into Samba on the edge of the box. He lays off to McAidoo, but his shot goes sailing over the bar.

A surprise to no one, it is chucking it down in Manchester.

Big cheers from the away end as Norwich get their first corner of the evening. It is lofted high and long to the back post, where it is headed away by Bouaddi. It bounces out to Musaba, who has just come on, and he strikes it from the top of the box on the half-volley.

His shot cuts through a crowd in the box and has Rulli diving to his left, but it goes wide of the post. What an introduction that would have been!

Well all the stories from this match will be all about young Floyd Samba. Feel free to leave your best punny Samba/dance-related headlines in the comments section.

For Man City as you would expect it is all about game management from here on out.

Some more changes to report for Norwich as well, as Crnac is replaced by Musaba.

Wright is able to run in to space towards the edge of the box, but as has been their story all evening, his pass out to the wing is just not where it needs to be and their effort just breaks down.

What a way to score a second! A night to remember for Floyd Samba!

Norwich try and play out from the back but far too sloppy and Ait-Nouri picks up the ball on the left of the box. He has plenty of time to tee up Samba inside the box at the left corner, who finds himself with plenty of space to curl his shot into the far corner, beating the diving Grimshaw.

We may be seeing plenty more of him this season.

Norwich looking for their way back into the game, as the ball comes down the left, fizzed in low and flashes past Rulli, trying to claim it. It deflects off a crowd of bodies and spins up, but Fisher can’t connect and it spins away harmlessly wide of the goal.

It is definitely Norwich’s best chance of the game and Fisher will be upset he hasn’t made more of that.

And Allan makes it three! Minutes after the restart, the Brazilian makes his own mark on his debut.

Maresca switched him onto the left side to escape Yongwa, and he picks up the ball outside the box and makes the run inside. He runs circles around Field and slots the ball home into the far bottom corner.

Some changes from both sides at half-time. McAidoo comes on for Cherki, though O’Reilly is the one to move up into midfield to fill the gap.

45 minutes left for the visitors to create something special!

What a moment for Floyd Samba! 😍A goal on his Man City debut for the 17-year-old, son of former Blackburn defender Chris 🩵 pic.twitter.com/VCVfX9HCNn

Manchester City will be the ones to host Brighton in the next round – giving the visitors the opportunity to pull off a remarkable feat of knocking out both Manchester sides should they win.

Enjoy the highlights from last night as they came from behind to dispatch Man Utd:

And without much ado at the end of the half, we have reached the break. City put themselves in control with two quick-fire goals and it looks a tall task for Norwich to find their way back into the match.

Credit where it is due, Yongwa has been very good for Norwich. He has stood fast, made some very good challenges and stopped Allan getting much of a look-in on the right.

As we approach half-time, the stats tell a sorry story. Norwich have had just 28% possession and created a single shot, none on target.

As City come again, Norwich have pulled every man back to try and keep the situation salvageable before the break.

Samba was in again there, making a run into the box with a ball from Cherki, wrestling with Bruno Alves as he goes. The defender does enough to throw him off and Grimshaw is able to come out and snatch the ball.

Man City are looking to close this out now, and they look threatening every time they break.

Ait-Nouri is the latest to try his luck, making a run into the box from the left, but his shot is blocked.

A few minutes to remember here for Floyd Samba. First he steers home a very well taken header to give City the lead and then he plays a crucial role in the second, holding the ball up well before laying it off to Bouaddi to release Cherki to score. That’s how to make an impression on your debut.

And the floodgates have opened. Two goals in two minutes for the defending champions.

Samba finds Bouaddi in midfield, who takes it forward and feeds Cherki running to his left. He gets himself one-on-one and slots cool as you like into the bottom left corner.

City are in control all of a sudden and Norwich will be devastated.

As soon as I say that, Floyd Samba finds a way through.

He has looked the brightest for City, and O’Reilly sends a cross over the box from the left, drawing Grimshaw away from position. The ball is pinged back in by Allan and the youngster stoops to meet it, heading in to the bottom corner.

Norwich have been very disciplined in defence so far. Yongwa has been closing down Allan on the wing very well.

Cherki is starting to get some momentum – but is swarmed by yellow shirts as he picks up the ball on the edge of the area.

Another loose ball from City in midfield and Norwich pick it up again. The ball to set the front line free is equally as loose from the visitors though and it breaks down once again.

Samba is looking lively, racing to get on a ball in front of Darling just on the edge of the box. Darling recovers to send it out for a corner, which becomes a free kick after Ait-Nouri wrestles his man to the ground at the back post as City are taking.

Wright sends a long ball across the field, looking for a man on the right side but Rulli is alert to it and comes to claim at the edge of the box.

Kovacic shows some promise with a strong run on the ball down the centre of the field, taking the ball all the way to the edge of the box, where he collides with a defender, and the ball spins away for Norwich to clear out.

This is better from City, who have looked like they’re lacking drive so far.

Yongwa again probing down the left side. It takes two to dispossess him and Man City manage to get the throw in, but approaching 20 minutes Norwich will be happy with this.

Kovacic loses the ball in midfield and Norwich surge forward. The move breaks down as Wright’s pass to Diallo on the wing is just behind him and he can’t take it forward into the box.

Spent the first 10 minutes trying to work out City’s system and settled on a 3-1-5-1, with Bouaddi operating as a nominal third centre-back, but it seems to have changed again now with O’Reilly dropping to left back and Bouaddi stepping into midfield. No doubt the metamorphosis will continue.

This Man City team have never played all together and it is clear that they’re still settling in here, figuring out how they’re going to press here.

Kovacic in the captain’s armband is tying it all together in midfield.

Khusanov threads a lovely ball to Samba who flicks it into the path of Lewis, who takes it and makes a run into the box. He creates space and sends a right-footed shot over the bar – but Man City are building.

Norwich make a move forward, with Yongwa bringing the ball down the left side but his cross into the box is blocked by Allan sliding in. The Brazilian is then fouled again as Yongwa tries to reclaim the ball and Man City get back in possession.

It’s actually three Samba brothers at City. The youngest, Emerson, is also in the academy.

Early foul on Allan gets Man City a free kick and they have started as everyone expected they would – in plenty of possession.

They look for the early goal as O’Reilly feeds him in the from the left side, but the shot is blocked.

With just over 10 minutes until kick-off here are the teams for tonight’s fixture:

Man City XI: Rulli; O’Reilly, Vitor Reis, Khusanov, Lewis; Kovacic (c), Bouaddi; Ait-Nouri, Cherki, Allan; Samba

Subs: Anderson, Braithwaite, Donnarumma, Fernández, Guéhi, McAidoo, Ndiaye, Matheus Nunes, Semenyo

Norwich City XI: Grimshaw; Yongwa, Bruno Alves, Darling (c), Fisher; Field, Wright; Diallo, Ben Slimane, Crnac; Kvistgaarden

Subs: Chrisene, Mattsson, Kovacevic, Maghoma, McConville, Musaba, Schwartau, Stacey, Touré

"It's part of the decision that I took when I decided to join this club"Enzo Maresca responds to the doubts surrounding him filling Pep Guardiola's shoes 👇 pic.twitter.com/o6eUjQUOnU

David 🆚 Goliath 🤝🎥 https://t.co/5YXw2tQvfX pic.twitter.com/fTp9zD0xiX

As Abdukodir Khusanov makes his fourth start of the season, Hugo Viana, Man City director of football, has been speaking about the young Uzbek. The 22-year-old signed a new five-year contract with City in July, and Viana has affirmed that he “will be one of the best centre-backs in the world”.

"Abdukodir Khusanov will be one of the best centre-backs in the world" - Hugo Viana 🇺🇿🌏Full interview 🔗 https://t.co/dk3Qi8DF8D pic.twitter.com/hHdVdX5HSF

It’s nine changes for Norwich from the squad that lost 4-3 to Middlesbrough on the weekend.

Norwich goalkeeper Daniel Grimshaw came through the ranks at Manchester City, joining as a teenager, so this will be a special night for the 28-year-old.

Speaking of Phil Foden, the winger will not be making an appearance tonight, as he is serving his three-match suspension following his sending off in the Manchester derby. The England international lashed out at Bruno Fernandes after the United captain had fouled him, resulting in a red card for violent conduct.

As well as this fixture, he will also be missing City’s game against Sunderland and the trip to Anfield to face Liverpool the following weekend.

We broke down the incident as it happened on Sunday and you can get the full story here

Heavy squad rotation (10 changes in total for Maresca) has handed debuts for Gero Rulli in goal, as well as Allan and Floyd Samba in the outfield.

17-year-old Samba is the latest from City’s academy to be making his debut in the senior squad, following in the footsteps of Phil Foden, Rico Lewis, Nico O’Reilly and many more. A versatile midfielder, he has totalled 24 appearances across six competitions (incl Premier League 2) and scored 17 and assisted six goals in those matches.

Keep your eyes on young midfielder Floyd Samba, who has been handed his Manchester City debut tonight against Norwich by manager Enzo Maresca. Floyd is the 17 year old son of former Blackburn Rovers defender Christopher Samba.

His older brother Tyrone, 18, also plays for City. The siblings played in City’s FA Youth Cup final win over Manchester United last season, with Floyd scoring the first in a 2-1 win.

City fans will also be keen to see how Allan Elias gets on on his first start, having arrived from Palmeiras for £34m. Geronimo Rulli also debuts in goal.

Checking in 🚌🚶‍♂️ pic.twitter.com/xWYGyaH7TY

Ⓒ Darling with the armband🧤 Grimshaw in goal⚡️ Ante on the rightYour Yellows for this evening ⬇️ pic.twitter.com/znOGtvyJyk

Your City side to take on Norwich 👊XI | Rulli, Lewis, Khusanov, Reis, O'Reilly, Bouaddi, Kovačić (C), Samba, Allan, Aït-Nouri, CherkiSUBS | Donnarumma, Anderson, Guéhi, Ndiaye, Fernández, Nunes, Semenyo, McAidoo, Braithwaite🤝 @etihad pic.twitter.com/LCA4WfACBf

Good evening and welcome to another night of Carabao Cup coverage! It is the final fixture of round three (I promise) as Manchester City host Norwich.

These two sides have not met since 2022, when Norwich were still in the top flight and were beaten 4-0 by City. Looking at their previous meetings, the odds are definitely stacked in favour of Enzo Maresca’s side, who have scored 14 unanswered goals in their last three meetings with Norwich, while the Championship side have not scored any.

City will be looking to make it six straight wins across all competitions tonight, having started perfectly in the Premier League with four wins from four, and comfortably seeing off Porto in their Champions League opener.

They were the talk of the weekend with their deeply controversial 1-0 win over rivals Manchester United as – having gone down to 10 men after Phil Foden was sent off – their winning goal was allowed to stand despite Enzo Fernández being clearly in an offside position that impacted United’s keeper and backline.

Erling Haaland has put Manchester City ahead in the derby after a VAR check ⚽️ pic.twitter.com/V0DCwryhFy

City are defending their title in this competition – beating Arsenal last year in the final – but like all Premier League teams playing in European competitions, have only entered the tournament this year in the third round.

#1639. Frosinone boss Alvini content with aggressive approach vs. Milan despite ‘naive’ mistakes

Frosinone head coach Massimiliano Alvini has admitted that his side simply gave AC Milan too many opportunities.

It has been a very positive return to the top flight for Frosinone so far, given that a point last night at San Siro would have seen them move back into the European places. However, they were ultimately given a bit of a humbling by Milan, who won 5-1 thanks to a ruthless counter-attacking display.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

Some have questioned if the Canarini were a bit too aggressive in their approach to the game, given they played with such a high line and allowed space for Adrien Rabiot, Diego Moreira, Goncalo Ramos, Ardon Jashari, Alphadjo Cisse and Christian Pulisic to exploit.

Alvini was present in the press conference room at San Siro after the full-time whistle and he analysed what was perhaps the most difficult night of the season for his team. MilanNews transcribed his assessments.

Should the game have been played differently?

“Frosinone played their game but made a few mistakes they don’t usually make, but that’s certainly not my concern, losing by such a large margin. What’s worrying are the mistakes we made that we could have avoided.”

“We made a mistake on the first goal, which was a mistake of our own, while the other goals we conceded were goals we absolutely could have avoided. We conceded them and were naive.

“It’s a mistake of our own, and so today, from this perspective, if you come to Milan against Milan and make these mistakes, it’s only natural that we end up losing like this, by such a large scoreline.

“That’s the analysis, even though I think the scoreline is even too large: the first half, in my opinion, was extraordinary on our part.”

Did the absences have an impact, forcing you to experiment a bit?

“There’s nothing experimental about it. We played with the same principles, running forward to get to Rabiot. We preferred to bring on a defender who would push forward rather than a midfielder.

“In my opinion, this definitely didn’t influence the result, but rather the attitude, the idea, or the match strategy. And we certainly made – as I said before and I’ll repeat – mistakes we don’t usually make.

“If you give Milan certain chances, with such strong players and the quality of this team, you risk losing, and that’s what happened. You risk losing with a heavy defeat, and that’s what happened.

“He had a problem with that back heel in the box, and he definitely needs tests. It’s too early now; we’ll have to wait for the tests, which will be done starting Tuesday, but it’s definitely a problem.”

“We had a chance with Monterisi after a minute, we hit the post, and we created a lot. I have nothing to say to the team for their attitude and the way they played.

“We, I repeat, made some naivety, some mistakes. It’s also up to me to understand that there are important players on the other side who can cause problems.”

“It’s a result that definitely needs to be managed, navigated, and channeled, but it doesn’t change my attitude at all. We have 20 points today. The path we need to take is to try to stay in Serie A, and we’ll try to do so with this attitude, with this identity: this is the path we’ll take.

“Four years ago, I drew a game against Milan by playing defensively, and we took home a point. Today we made some mistakes, but this is the path we’ll take. I’m happier with the management, with the team’s identity, to try to achieve that objective, and this is what we’ll continue to do.”

#1638. Ex-Man United star Gordon Strachan tells Mauricio Pochettino what will get the Red Devils out of current crisis

By Matt Law | 24 Nov 2026 20:30, Last updated: 24 Nov 2026 20:31

Manchester United need to show character as they attempt to bounce back in Wednesday's Champions League clash with Sporting Lisbon, ex-Red Devils midfielder Gordon Strachan has exclusively told Sports Mole.

The 20-time English champions will enter the European fixture with Sporting off the back of a 4-0 defeat to Liverpool in the Premier League.

Mauricio Pochettino will now take charge of his first European match for Man United, and there is pressure on the Argentine following the four-goal mauling at Anfield.

When asked whether the Sporting match provided Man United with the perfect chance to bounce back from the defeat to Liverpool, Strachan insisted that the players need to show character and heart in a bid to turn the club's campaign around.

"Well, to be fair, Liverpool should never really be a big ask for Man United as such, because the record there is terrific over the years. I mean, it's always been decent. That fixture is one of the ones that Liverpool really want to win because they know how dangerous Man United are," said Strachan.

"But it wasn't a real game after the first two goals, there was the sending-off, you know. And even the free kick, you think, right, if you see the free kick off, we can reorganise and organise with 10 players. We never even had time to do that. So, as a manager, you can't count that, you've just got to count that as a no-game.

"But what you can do in that situation is ask, who kept pressing? Who do I want in my team? Because in adversity, you see the real character coming out, and in adversity in big games, you see the real character. And it's not on your social media, it's not saying to the fans, we love you and we're sorry and all the rest of it. Don't apologise to me, just do something about it.

"Don't come in and hold your hand up and say, I'm sorry, gaffer. Don't apologise to me because I'm not interested in you telling me you're sorry for making a mistake. Just don't make a mistake. And if you do make a mistake, rectify it as quickly as possible.

"What I'm talking about is managers will try and sort it out. Invariably, unless you can do something about it, physically or mentally, then it will appear again. They will appear, and they'll appear in crisis moments.

"As I said, your character is shown up in crisis times and the same mistakes will be made by the same people whoever they play. And some people are just not good enough to play at this level.

"You know, we all talk about shapes and systems and this and that. The funny thing is, I don't think there's too many people talking about systems now. I think most people are now talking about, even if you talk with a bright manager, they talk about putting people under pressure, winning knockdowns, getting to the ball first, getting the ball to your front men.

"So, the system thing has kind of changed now. The only one that kind of really changes, it's gone from a back four to a back three, but the rest, like Brighton, Liverpool, Bournemouth, they're all playing the same sort of way.

"It's a kind of 4-2-3-1, where the four players up front are attacking players, whatever way you want to use it, two wide men, just off the front. Wales were the same with Craig Bellamy.

"So, I think that people are moving to that in general now, but there's not too much talking about systems now. It's more about closing down, getting to knockdowns, winning headers and free kicks and corner kicks."

Man United have six points to show from their two matches in the league stage of this season's Champions League.

Gordon Strachan was speaking to Sports Mole on behalf of William Hill Football Odds.

#1637. Man City are failing to give their supporters something to stand behind as Enzo Maresca's side radiate uncertainty with meek display in Fulham draw, writes JACK GAUGHAN

Published: 11:04 EST, 21 November 2026 | Updated: 14:16 EST, 21 November 2026

The bananas are disappearing now winter is coming, the fire and fury waning with each passing week. In legal limbo, Manchester City’s supporters need something – anything – to stand behind but increasingly their team refuse to provide that solace.

City were booed off at the end as Enzo Maresca ducked down the tunnel. Some of that could have been directed at referee Thomas Bramall, after Erling Haaland’s disallowed goal, but certainly a significant number were jeering what they’d just seen. That simply does not happen at the Etihad Stadium, even during the torrid run of two years ago.

But they are witnessing a squad who radiate uncertainty. Who take three touches when two will do; who always receive possession squarely facing their own goal; who do not create passing lines for their mates. And crucially, who are forever momentarily confused as to who exactly is picking up which runner and those split seconds make all the difference in this division.

There is just this strange state of unease around how they want to approach games at the moment, something that adversity can provoke and something that Maresca is adamant he can correct. A coach of his calibre should do given the time and freedom.

Yet when he spent the two-week international break studying clips and fashioning ways of improving, he cannot have envisaged a scenario whereby home fans were so incredulous at a lack of energy that they were roused to their feet when Haaland deigned to close down Bernd Leno and force an error.

Man City put in an underwhelming performance as they were held to a 1-1 draw by Fulham

Enzo Maresca's side are radiating uncertainty and look worryingly vulnerable at the back

Rodrigo Muniz made City pay as he put an impressive Fulham 1-0 ahead after 16 minutes

Fulham popped it about nicely and at will. Found pockets to hurt their illustrious hosts, who were again asking a centre half – in this case Marc Guehi – to charge into midfield. City did have more balance than at Nottingham Forest for including Ayyoub Bouaddi for Enzo Fernandez, yet Alvaro Arbeloa still aggressively pressed them in that area to some success.

‘I told the players that we will have the chance to beat them if we play with courage,’ said Arbeloa, who was indebted to the towering performance of defender David Affengruber.

Arsenal will have watched this grinning and could easily be racking up an unassailable lead once these teams meet in north London next Sunday. Unassailable with all the usual caveats about the appeal and what this season may or may not eventually mean.

City did create enough statistically but as with other games of late, that did not tell the whole story.

Calvin Bassey pirouetted through midfield, the heavily derided Gianluigi Donnarumma thwarting a number of strong Fulham chances, and City appeared somewhat lost and out of ideas.

Elliot Anderson equalised with a superb volley but City failed to create much after that

Maresca expressed his concern at City's lack of clean sheets after they struggled again

That is a worrying departure from recent defeats, where they attacked with the same abandon as that early season flourish when they might as well have hosted games at Madison Square Gardens and played with an orange ball.

MAN CITY (4-2-3-1): Donnarumma 7; Khusanov 6, Dias 6, Guehi 5, O’Reilly 5 (Gvardiol 78); Anderson 7, Bouaddi 7 (Fernandez 85); Ndiaye 6 (Allan 78), Foden 7 (Cherki 70), Doku 5; Haaland 5

FULHAM (4-2-3-1): Leno 6; Tete 6, Affengruber 8, Bassey 7, Sessegnon 7 (Palacios 83); Berge 6, Charles 7; Bobb 7 (Garcia 78), King 6 (Larsson 70, 6), Iwobi 7 (Robinson 70, 6); Muniz 7 (Cairney 83)

Met with a Fulham who had not conceded more than once in the league since the start of September, City failed to create a meaningful opportunity in the last 25 minutes of a match they were desperate to win and should have been in the ascendancy of after Elliot Anderson’s volleyed equaliser after half time.

Maresca, though, is more concerned with a lack of clean sheets. It’s now none of those in nine games in all competitions for the first time in seven years, with Rodrigo Muniz opening the scoring on 16 minutes. A throw inside Fulham’s own third prompted Guehi to jump and lose his duel, City turned around and Oscar Bobb laid on for Muniz.

‘We’re conceding too many goals,’ Maresca said. ‘We need to avoid it. You need to win games 1-0. You need clean sheets. We’re not able to do it. But I can see many positive aspects. We started four months ago and not four years ago.

‘We’ve conceded almost 80 per cent of our goals at the start of the first half and second half. It’s something we need to improve. It’s a throw in at the corner flag and nobody is expecting they can create something.’

Maresca was also insistent that Haaland ought to have been awarded an equaliser before the break when poking in on the goal line, yet Bramall adjudged that Leno had the ball under control on field, with VAR not overruling.

Some hard luck, some profligacy with Haaland squandering a couple of big chances, but the day was summed up when in stoppage time, Jeremy Doku was penalised for a foul throw.

After narrowly missing out on booking their place in the UEFA Champions League for the second consecutive year last season, finishing fifth in Ligue 1 and just one point below Lyon in fourth, Marseille will be extremely disappointed with how they have performed on the continent so far this campaign.

Although they edged out Leverkusen in their latest Europa League fixture, losses to Sturm Graz, Olympiacos and Besiktas in each of their opening three matches mean Bruno Genesio’s men have earned just three points so far in Europe, leaving them 31st in the league phase table and outside of the knockout stage places.

Despite conceding two late goals to lose against Le Mans on Sunday evening, Les Olympiens have seen a huge improvement in their league endeavours, having won each of their prior five matches to currently sit fifth in the Ligue 1 table and just three points outside the automatic Champions League qualification places.

Marseille are yet to claim victory over Levski, though they do boast a mainly positive record against Bulgarian opposition, having beaten CSKA Sofia in each of their other two meetings with efbet League sides.

Having won their first efbet League title since 2009 last season and finished 10 points ahead of runners-up Ludogorets, who had triumphed in each of the previous 14 consecutive campaigns, Levski competed in the qualifying stages of the Champions League for the first time in 17 years during the summer.

The Blues impressed in their efforts for tournament qualification, beating Borac Banja Luka, Univ Craiova and Kairat Almaty to progress to the decisive playoff tie, but having endured a 4-0 aggregate defeat against Greek giants AEK Athens, the Bulgarian side are instead competing in the Europa League this season.

However, Julio Velazquez’s men have given a good account of themselves so far on the continent as after taking just one point from their first two matches, Levski have won back-to-back matches in the Europa League to sit 10th in the standings with seven points and only outside the round-of-16 positions on goal difference.

While the Blues do not have the best recent record against French opposition, having won just one of their previous four meetings with Ligue 1 sides, that triumph did come over Marseille, with Levski securing a 1-0 win over Les Olympiens in the group stages of this competition in December 2005, when it was branded as the UEFA Cup.

#1633. The virtues of patience

It’s 13 December 2020. Arsenal versus Burnley.

It was freezing and wet at the Emirates. Only 2,000 fans had been allowed in because of Covid, and my mum, my dad, my mate Ben and I made up four of them. We were socially distanced and wearing masks. My glasses kept steaming up.

This was supposed to be fun. Watching my team.

Willian was grotesquely slow. Alex Lacazette was profligate. Rob Holding was bald. Very bald. And Granit Xhaka was angry. So angry, in fact, that in the second half he put his hands around the throat of some opposition goon and, after a VAR review, got himself sent off. There were boos. As many as 2,000 people could muster, anyway.

Then our captain, Pierre Emerick-Aubameyang, headed a corner into his own net. You couldn’t make it up. Except you could. It was the only goal of the game.

By then the steam fogging up my specs might as well have been coming out of my ears. In his player ratings, Andrew M called Xhaka the ‘King of the Idiots’ and described the match and the result as ‘utterly shit’. Which was fair.

It was our seventh defeat in 10 league games and our fourth in a row at home, something that hadn’t happened since 1953. We were 15th, five points above the relegation zone.

And who was top? Sp*rs. Managed by everyone’s favourite sociopath, Jose Mourinho. Having beaten us in the North London derby the week before, they couldn’t stop gloating.

I’d bought into the Arteta project hook, line and sinker. I still wanted him to be the right man for the job. I was just finding it harder to explain why I thought he was. The FA Cup win had been four months earlier. It felt like years.

The tree, to paraphrase our manager, was shaking.

It had been shaking for a good two and a half years by then. The soggy bottom of the Arsene Wenger era had left its scars. Those two 3-0 defeats to City in the space of a week still make me wince. Then came the hope that Unai Emery might get us back on track. By the time we’d seen how that played out, I’d got into the habit of talking myself down whenever things looked up. Maybe we’ll get better. Give it time.

The trouble with rock bottom is you never know if there’s another floor below it. Was Burnley ours? I’m still writing about it six years later, so it was probably mine. There were games against Southampton and Everton before Christmas, and I can barely remember either of them.

Then came Boxing Day and a visit from Frank Lampard’s Chelsea. Is it reductive to say that was the day everything changed for Mikel Arteta’s Arsenal? Probably. But my word, watching Bukayo Saka, Emile Smith Rowe and Gabriel Martinelli tear about the place was the fix this addict needed. We went on an unbeaten run after that. Seven whole games! And for the first time in weeks, I was looking forward to what came next.

And here we are in November 2026. Reigning champions of England. Top of the league again. Five points clear. Odds-on favourites to retain the title after 10 games. Sure, throwing hundreds of millions of American dollars at the problem helped. But if there’s a lesson in all this, it’s that hard work and patience pay off.

Which is why I’m using today’s blog to appeal directly to Sir Jim Ratcliffe to give Michael Carrick a stay of execution.

Come on, man, you’re probably still paying off Erik ten Hag and Ruben Amorim, maybe even Ralf Rangnick. Do you really want to go back to the drawing board all over again? Carrick is the man for the Manchester United hot seat. Just look at the way he wore a poppy-embroidered armband as well as a poppy badge at the weekend. The man doesn’t do half measures. He’s a two-scoops guy. Surely that’s something you, a multibillionaire British-born petrochemicals tycoon who lives in Monaco, can get on board with?

I know Mauricio Pochettino might be tempting. He’s got floppy hair, a tan and, despite the Sp*rsy stench, has come to resemble a rather huggable teddy bear. But think it through, Jim. What if he comes in and everybody perks up? It’s much harder to make job cuts and to force out season ticket holders when people are enjoying themselves. Best get through that process first while Michael turns the oil tanker round. It’s not far off, promise, you’re on a two-game unbeaten streak!

Anyway, what would sacking Carrick say about patience? Look at Arteta. There were people who wanted him gone after Burnley and, as you’ve just read, I was close to joining them. Imagine if the club had listened to me. All those years of work, all that progress, all the joy I’ve had watching Arsenal lately. We could have thrown it all away because a man in a damp mask couldn’t see out of his glasses.

So give Carrick time. Give him January. Give him a full pre-season. And if things still haven’t picked up by this time next year, ask yourself whether one full pre-season, and £100 million on Youri Tielemans and Andrey Santos, was ever really enough.

I can only speak for myself, Jim, but I haven’t looked forward to watching Manchester United this much in years.

The Interlull kicks into gear tonight. David Raya, Mikel Merino and Martin Zubimendi are in action for Spain against Czechia, Riccardo Calafiori’s Italy take on France, and England face Croatia at Wembley.

Ezri Konsa and Myles Lewis-Skelly will both miss out at Wembley. Konsa is working on his fitness but will be available to face Spain on Sunday, while our Hale Ender is suspended after picking up two bookings in the Nations League.

Elsewhere, ahead of Sweden’s game against Bosnia and Herzegovina, Viktor Gyokeres has been speaking to the press. Like Martin Zubimendi, he says he’s happy at Arsenal.

“I want to,” he said, when asked if he’s keen to stay at the Emirates.

“It feels good when I’ve played. We’ve won most of the games. It was a tough loss in the cup (against Fleetwood). Otherwise it’s felt good for myself and the team, says the forward. I’ve been doing well lately when I’ve been playing. Right now it feels good.

“The communication with (Mikel) Arteta is good. We talk about football and how we should play. Before a match, if I’m going to start, we talk about the opponents and what I should think about.”

He was also asked whether the criticism he gets bothers him.

“Sometimes it might get to me, but overall not so much. If I score goals and assists in the Champions League, I couldn’t care less what they say. It’s nice to do those kinds of performances. To deliver for myself and for the team. That’s where the focus lies.”

To be fair, I’ve not seen any serious chatter about selling Viktor in January. Whatever you think of him as a player, it would be a strange move unless we’re planning to spend serious money on the attack. And even then it would feel like an unnecessary risk given Kai isn’t exactly pulling up trees and new faces will need an adaptation period.

If he’s happy keeping his head down and doing his bit for the team, I’d keep him around until the summer and reassess then.

Ok. I’m going to leave it there for today. All eyes on Old Trafford, I guess.
