Tyrick Mitchell's opener is disallowed for an offside in the build up! ❌ pic.twitter.com/7y975TxaUj

Liverpool give up possession in Bournemouth’s half and Christie strides forward releasing Rayan before continuing his run to the near post. The Brazilian picks out his team-mate but Christie gets too strong a contact on the ball and the ball sails wide.

Truffert passes the ball straight to Gakpo inside his own box but Adams is on the scene in a flash and snaps into a tackle and takes the ball away from the Liverpool forward.

The second has already settled into a holding pattern, with neither side creating much. Isak makes a run down the right hand side and, with players loaded in the box, he blasts the ball high into the sky and beyond his team-mates. That pretty much sums things up.

Wirtz has given the ball away twice in the first minute of the second half. Carragher is on Sky Sports commentary duties and he says he’s surprised to see him back out on the pitch.

Szoboszlai concedes a foul on the far side but the subsequent delivery is too heavy and sails over everyone.

No half-time changes from either manager.

Isak’s first-half heatmap makes for interesting reading. The good news, for Liverpool fans, is that he’s stationed himself predominantly in the final third. The bad news... those positions have been everywhere but the box.

There must be significant temptation to drift out to the wide areas and drop deep when the ball is not coming to you, but surely Liverpool need their No 9 closer to Bournemouth’s goal?

Big chance missed from Haaland of all people to make it 4-2 to City in what has been a pulsating, spell-binding first 45 minutes. It’s fast, furious and a helluva lot of fun to watch. Brilliant from Ndiaye to tee up Haaland who shoots wide of a post. A game for attackers shall we say ...

There are significant advantages to having a goalkeeper who is 6ft 5in with long arms and massive hands. Brobbey’s shot cannons off Guehi and would have looped over a number of goalkeeper but Donnarumma sticks out a giant arm to help nudge the ball over the bar and keep City 3-2 in front in the fifth minute of first half stoppages

Not a pretty half from the returning Iraola’s side, who will need to be much better in the second period to challenge for the three points.

Bournemouth have dropped points late on in a number of matches this season and will perhaps rue not being able to capitalise on their early advantage.

City are in front. Again. Semenyo this time, he fires the ball beyond Roefs having collected a loose ball int he box.

Antoine Semenyo gets his first goal of the season! 🎯 pic.twitter.com/1n2W5Cyxz0

A relatively slick Liverpool move sees the ball worked out to Araujo on the right who has minded to bomb on with increasing frequency, and while he’s able to win a corner, Szoboszlai’s delivery is cleared with a minimum of fuss.

Iraola came into this game saying that his side held an advantage having played two days earlier than Bournemouth in midweek. You would never have guessed it from what we have witnessed here today.

And right on cue, a frustrated Isak attempts a specultative effort from range which sails high and wide.

Sunderland are level again as Brobbey scores after lengthy VAR check for offside.

Sunderland fans sing “F--- VAR” and City fans boo the delay while they both awaited the verdict, which has now gone Sunderland’s way

Brian Brobbey levels it AGAIN! 🤯 pic.twitter.com/YvelzwnmY8

Can’t hold a lead today City. Wow, Sunderland are level again in an instant and it’s that man Brobbey again. There’s a VAR check going on to check for offside

So, this is not a rush to make a sweeping criticism, it’s simply an observation. But Liverpool fans will be looking at Bradley Barcola and  waiting to see that first burst, that moment of electricity, that has showed why they bought him. It’s like you look for a touch, a pass, a moment of skill. He’s just had a shot saved but it all seems very tentative for him at the moment. And that is what he needs - a moment.

Jacquet does brilliantly to close down Christie as the Scot was stealing into the box and looking to pull the trigger.

Chances! Barcola forces Petrovic into an awkward-looking save, before follow-up efforts from Wirtz and Gakpo are charged down.

Mac Allister is fouled 25 yards out moments later and Szoboszlai gets another go. Here, he drags his effort just wide.

It’s all happening at the Etihad. Cherki restores City’s lead with his third Premier League goal of the season.

It’s a great finish from Cherki to put City back in front but it doesn’t happen if Ndiaye is quick to read Danso’s risky pass and win possession. Sharp as a button in that moment.

Rayan Cherki puts Manchester City back in front! 💫 pic.twitter.com/PP4MAV9kw3

A really poor piece of defending from Kerkez gives Bournemouth a free-kick out on the right. Tavernier spins in an inswinger but Van Dijk heads clear. Truffert launches another assault on Liverpool’s box off the second phase but Alisson is wise to it and gathers.

It appears that Liverpool are beginning to settle, they take the opportunity to circulate the ball in front of Bournemouth’s first line of pressure, waiting for the right moment to pounce. The final pass is poor, though, and Araujo through-pass goes all the way through to Petrovic. It was aimed at Isak ...I think.

Some signs of life from Liverpool, as they create a substantial overload down their left, Kerkez, Mac Allister, Barcola and Isak meeting on that flank. Barcola attempts a sprint into the channel off the shoulder of the ball-side centre-back but he is deemed offside. Looked close, but a bit better from Liverpool.

Araujo has the chance to launch a long throw into the box but Silva beats Van Dijk to the summit and Petrovic gathers the loose ball.

Scott then sprays a wonderful ball over to Rayan on the right but his cutback to Tavernier comes to nothing after the midfielder loses the ball. Liverpool then spring a counter of their own, but Bournemouth recover and charge down a hopeful Gakpo effort from the edge of the box.

Liverpool will not be pleased with their start to this match. They’ve struggled to string more than three passes together without ceding possession and Isak has cut an isolated figure up top.

First time that Bournemouth have gone through the gears and the move ends with Alisson Becker saving brilliantly from Evanilson. It’s a funny stadium, here, as it can be quiet then all of a sudden a tempest whips up and you can sense the mood changing. Liverpool are struggling for alacrity and Andoni Iraola is keeping an eye on Florian Wirtz, who is moving gingerly after taking a bang to his left foot.

Some start at the Etihad. You had to wonder if a big early missed chance from Nilson Angulo was going to haunt Sunderland with City taking the lead just a few minutes later through a quite sublime free-kick from Enzo Fernandez. But Sunderland have immediately hit back. Maresca will decry the defending but it’s brilliant from Enzo Le Fee, who surges forward and then splits Nunes and Dias with an inch perfect pass that Brobbey takes beautifully in his stride before finishing.

On Fernandez’s free-kick before then, he’d very much shaped as if he’s going to cross the ball from a free-kick on the right side of the penalty area. The execution was immaculate but it was telling just how effectively he’d managed to deceive the Sunderland goalkeeper. It was world class

A slight mix-up sees Kerkez and Wirtz bump into each other by the touchline. The Germany international limps away and grimaces but should be fine to continue.

Chance! Alisson makes amends with a stunning save. Tavernier had hit the by-line and lasered a cross to Evanilson who, with the ball slightly behind him, improvised and flicked it toward the near post. Alisson gets down swiftly and turns behind for a corner which comes to nothing.

Jacquet gives away a needless foul on the near side but Scott’s delivery goes straight into Alisson’s hands. The Brazilian’s throw out is poor, though, and Scott darts into Liverpool’s box, just unable to pick out a team-mate.

Barcola is presented with green grass to run into, but just as he builds a head of steam Hill comes across in a flash and snuffs out the foray forward.

Woah, Brobbey responds immediately, stealing in between City defenders before slotting past Donnarumma.

Instant response from Sunderland as Brian Brobbey equalises! 💥 pic.twitter.com/et6AHGPAbl

Enzo Fernandez opens the scoring at the Etihad with a direct free-kick from out wide. Really poor from Roefs who was caught napping. That’s Fernandez’s first City goal.

Enzo Fernandez gets his first Manchester City goal in style! 🤩 pic.twitter.com/fVOnJvACYY

Wirtz earns a free-kick just outside the D. Bournemouth feel aggrieved as there looked to have been an earlier foul on Scott and to make matters worse Szoboszlai is standing over the ball.

His effort leaves Petrovic rooted to the spot but the ball veers just wide of the mark.

Evanilson’s willingness to drop deep is asking questions of Liverpool’s centre-backs. Do they follow him and risk disrupting their backline coverage?

The hosts attempt to work a short corner routine but Truffert’s eventual through-ball is too strong and the ball rolls out for a Liverpool goal-kick.

This wouldn’t go down as a fixture you would circle for being noteworthy but make no mistake this is a huge afternoon for Liverpool. They have had some days at the Vitality Stadium in recent years and last season’s defeat put a huge dent in Arne Slot’s hopes of trying to find a revival. It’s also a big test for Bournemouth, coming down from the euphoria of beating Real Sociedad. Let’s see how it all transpires.

Evanilson makes a smart run into the right channel and while Jacquet gets his foot on the ball he’s instantly smothered by Scott and the ball goes out for a Liverpool goal-kick. A sign of how high both sides will be willing to jump in search of the ball.

Both sides will look to force mistakes out of the other and Szoboszlai is able to pick Adams’ pocket on the halfway line. He offloads to Araujo who runs into a cul de sac down the right flank.

We are under way at the Vitality. Bournemouth are in their customary black-and-red home shirts kicking from right to left and Liverpool are in their white away kit and red shorts.

The players have emerged from the tunnel, Van Dijk and Smith at the front of the lines. A few pyrotechnics add to the atmosphere but one thing missing is the accidental sitting in the wrong dugout from the returning Iraola. He knows where he’s going.

Andoni Iraola returns to Bournemouth this weekend knowing what to expect from players he understands so well. Sadly, I do not mean Liverpool’s.

Having built his reputation creating a hard-working, well-drilled team rich in potential, Iraola is responsible for infusing those same characteristics into the most expensively assembled squad in Liverpool history.

His first six games demonstrate it is no quick fix. The Basque coach is the first Liverpool appointment to work with more than £700m of recent signings while being entitled to feel he has been dealt a bad hand.

Everything Iraola has said and done so far screams that he is searching for the right blend in his starting XI while having to eradicate negative traits, with and without the ball. It was telling that the excellent performance of his youngsters against Tottenham Hotspur in midweek offered the clearest hint of Iraola’s vision than anything we have seen with all the high-priced stars on the pitch.

There is a reason the Kop stood to acclaim the energy and application of youngsters Lewis Koumas, James McConnell and Trey Nyoni – and why Iraola keeps name-checking them. Iraola is indebted to them for issuing a reminder of the non-negotiables that come with being a Liverpool footballer; regardless of price tag and reputation, leaving everything on the pitch is compulsory. It is a concern that so many of the renowned players need to hear that message.

Jurgen Klopp named Florian Wirtz in his first squad as Germany manager and has said that fans must refrain from expecting “special moments” from the Liverpool playmaker as a matter of course.

Of Wirtz, he said: “I think he’s the player who covered the most ground at Liverpool this season, so the willingness is absolutely there.

“We have to move away from the idea that we need to see special moments from him. He is there to help us as a team. We have to make sure that Flo feels comfortable with us.”

Wirtz has delivered seven goals and 11 assists in his 54 Liverpool appearances.

Adam Smith, 35, played for Iraola 81 times and he admitted his former manager’s visit to the Vitality will be a sentimental affair. He said: “It’s going to be an emotional day for everyone I think, [for] our ex-manager and some of our players that have played under him, but we’ll be up for the game for sure.”

Bournemouth signed Truffert from Rennes in the summer of 2025 to replace Kerkez – who had just joined Liverpool – and the left-back has been a revelation at the Vitality. So much so that this week he earned himself a call-up to Zinedine Zidane’s first France squad.

Truffert topped the charts for most overlapping runs by any player in Europe’s top five leagues last season and laid on five assists.

Speaking before his return to the South Coast, Iraola said: “I know where we are going [the Vitality], and I know the stats they have there [unbeaten in 12 matches], not only in their stadium, overall, I think if you see the games they’ve lost in a long while, you realise how difficult it is to beat Bournemouth.

“But, I suppose I also have the advantage that I know them very well, they also have the advantage that they know me very well, so you never know who has more advantage in that sense.

He added: “On a personal side, I’m very much looking forward to meet them [his former players], to hug them. It’s players that I love, staff that I’ve been working with who I appreciate so much, and I was pushing for them [against Real Sociedad] when they were playing their first European game. I wish them all the best, but there is another part, which is the most important one right now that we need to go there and win.”

Good afternoon and welcome to our live coverage of the Premier League match between Liverpool and Bournemouth as Andoni Iraola returns to the Vitality Stadium for the first time since his big move up north. The Basque propelled Bournemouth to new heights, guiding the club into Europe and his successor, Marco Rose, ensured they made a winning start to life on the Continent by defeating Real Sociedad in midweek.

Previewing Iraola’s Vitality Stadium return, Craig Beazley, host and creator of the Up The Cherries In All Departments podcast, said: “We’ve now got the Andoni Iraola return … Andoni is very much a legend really, there should be a statue of Sir Eddie Howe and Sir Andoni Iraola [outside the ground] as well.”

Across three seasons, Iraola guided Bournemouth to 12th, ninth and sixth in the Premier League, winning 47 of his 127 matches in charge (37 per cent).

Liverpool are still acclimatising to his exacting style of play and their results suggest as much. They are 10th in the table having drawn three and won one, impressing in flashes but struggling to maintain consistently productive final-third patterns and pressing structures. Deploying Ronald Araújo at right-back has proved effective, though, with Liverpool conceding just two goals in their last four matches.

The Cherries are searching for their first Premier League win of the season and have retained the 4-2-3-1 shape from the Iraola days, with Rose preferring a similarly vertical attacking strategy. They continue to leverage their strengths in transitions and in wide areas as Adrien Truffert rains in crosses for any one of Bournemouth’s exuberant frontline to pounce on.

Elsewhere, Manchester City welcome Sunderland, who also secured a Europa League win during the week, to the Etihad while in-form Leeds United host Crystal Palace knowing a win would lift them into the top four.

#1550. Leeds transfer news: Will Lankshear January hopes shot down by 44-goal striker

By Ben Knapton | 25 Nov 2026 11:33

Former Leeds United striker Brian Deane, speaking exclusively to Sports Mole, has played down the Whites' chances of signing Will Lankshear in the January transfer window.

The former Tottenham Hotspur youngster has taken the Championship by storm since moving to the Riverside Stadium in the summer, scoring 14 goals in 15 second-tier appearances.

Lankshear netted the winner as Middlesbrough beat Swansea City 2-1 on Tuesday night, a result that saw Kim Hellberg's men move one point clear of Wolverhampton Wanderers at the top of the Championship table.

The 21-year-old unsurprisingly sits top of the Championship top scorers charts, three clear of closest challenger Andri Gudjohnsen of Blackburn Rovers in the race for the Golden Boot.

Lankshear's form has inevitably led to speculation surrounding a swift return to the Premier League, with multiple clubs believed to be interested in securing his services, including Leeds.

Former club Tottenham, Arsenal, Brighton & Hove Albion and Newcastle United have also been credited with an interest, although Middlesbrough's £70m asking price could deter suitors.

Now, former Leeds forward Deane - who scored 44 goals in 199 matches for the Whites - has expressed his view that Lankshear should remain at the Riverside Stadium over the winter.

“This is his breakout season, and he is at a good club," Deane told Sports Mole. "Middlesbrough look on course to challenge for promotion, so hopefully he gets there with them.

“He will be ambitious and attract attention from clubs such as Leeds, Brighton and Newcastle. He would be a good addition to a squad. But for his own development, I think he is in a good place at Middlesbrough.”

Lankshear made just six senior appearances for Tottenham before being sold in a £9.8m deal over the summer, and the striker's contract with Middlesbrough does not expire until 2031.

A young striker scoring for fun in the Championship will always attract glances from top-tier clubs, but Lankshear may struggle to force his way into Daniel Farke's first XI right now.

First-choice pairing Dominic Calvert-Lewin and Noah Okafor boast a respectable nine Premier League goals between them in 2026-27, and as long as both are fit, they will spearhead Farke's 3-5-2 system.

Calvert-Lewin is now in the final 24 months of his contract at Elland Road, but the England international is understood to be close to signing a new Leeds deal.

Lukas Nmecha also provides a steady backup option, although he is due to become a free agent in 2027 and may seek a move away in January if his game-time situation does not improve.

However, Nmecha's proposed exit would then open the door for summer signing Jean-Matteo Bahoya to earn more opportunities, so a winter move for Lankshear would make little sense for all involved.

Brian Deane was speaking to Sports Mole on behalf of BetWright.

#1549. Co-owner Brittany Mahomes leads wild celebrations as Kansas City Current wins NWSL title

Published: 09:15 EST, 22 November 2026 | Updated: 09:15 EST, 22 November 2026

Kansas City Current co-owner Brittany Mahomes led the celebrations as the women's soccer club won its first ever NWSL Championship on Saturday.

Brittany, the wife of Kansas City Chiefs quarterback Patrick Mahomes, was at Audi Field in Washington, DC for the final match of the season between the Current and the Washington Spirit.

A thrilling finish to the contest resulted in a 2-1 win for the Current, who have only been in existence for five years.

Brittany, who is pregnant with her fourth child, was seen on the pitch celebrating after her team's inaugural title.

She was seen embracing her team and her co-owners as they jumped up and down in celebration of the achievement.

Brittany was a part of the inaugural ownership group of the club when it was announced as an expansion team in 2020.

KC Current co-owner Brittany Mahomes celebrated her team winning the NWSL title

She was seen jumping up and down and celebrating with the players as the title was clinched

It's the first championship for the expansion club, which began playing in 2021

Brittany's husband, Kansas City Chiefs quarterback Patrick Mahomes, also celebrated the achievement on social media.

The three-time Super Bowl champion reshared the club's announcement on X, adding, 'AHHHHHHHHHH!!!!!!!!!!' He later added, 'LETS GOOOO!!!!!!' and a string of light blue hearts.

Kansas City went ahead in the match in the 54th minute with an 'Olimpico' goal from Vanessa DiBernardo, who watched her corner kick curl to the opposite post to break a first-half deadlock.

With Washington pressing late in added time, the Current were able to score on a counter attack goal from the foot of Brazilian star Debinha to make it 2-0.

Mere seconds later, Washington's Trinity Rodman scored a goal of her own to briefly give Spirit fans hope of a miraculous comeback.

But after 11 elapsed minutes - well beyond the nine given, thanks in part to a scary collision between Rodman and KC keeper Laney Rouse - the final whistle blew as Kansas City clinched the title.

The win for the Current means yet another season of heartbreak for Washington, who have made the last three straight NWSL Championship games and have lost all three.

#1548. Opinion: Andoni Iraola will start 'outstanding' attacker vs Club Brugge

Liverpool have performed much better since they were beaten by Fenerbahce in the Champions League a few weeks ago.

The Reds were torn apart by the Turkish Super Lig outfit with former Liverpool star Dirk Kuyt leading his team to a historic win.

Indeed, they are one of the better teams in Turkey but, compared to how much talent the Reds have among their ranks, they shouldn't have even had a chance to beat them.

That's why Liverpool's defeat was so hard to take for fans.

However, as mentioned, since then, things have gone well for Liverpool with the club even beating arch-rivals Manchester United 4-0.

Even though transfers are expected to occur in the January transfer window, Andoni Iraola still has a few players among his ranks who fans haven't seen the best of yet.

That's why Wednesday's Champions League tie against Club Brugge could be incredibly important for one of them.

Victor Munoz has to start against Club Brugge

Sunday's game was Liverpool's highlight of the season so far.

Their win against the Red Devils meant that they were thrusted back into fourth position and now find themselves seven points adrift of first-placed Arsenal.

This is still a decent gap to cut down but, it's a lot less daunting than the nine points that separated them over the international break.

During Sunday's victory against Man United, Victor Munoz was left on the bench to start with.

And, even though Liverpool were winning their arch-rivals 3-0 when the last 20 minutes of the game came upon them, Iraola still chose to bring the Spaniard on.

Most people expected that transfer to have been done to give those who started a rest but, Munoz had other plans.

In the 18 minutes of football that he played, his lightning quick speed and his ability to turn nothing chances into goals paid off as the 23-year-old bagged the Reds' fourth and last goal of the game.

He also maintained a 92 per cent pass accuracy and he even made one key pass.

This performance alone proves why he should be starting against Club Brugge in Liverpool's next Champions League tie.

Victor Munoz could become a key player for Liverpool in the next couple of years

Munoz was Liverpool's bargain signing of the summer transfer window.

The Spaniard was brought in by the Reds for a fee worth around £35 million.

At the time, Newcastle were also trying to sign him but, in the end, he chose Liverpool.

Most fans thought that he'd be more of a back-up than anything else but, in reality, he's become a key member of Iraola's first-team squad.

His performances have been second to none and, even though he's often been used in his less preferred position of right-wing, he's still contributed to four goals in the 13 games he's featured in.

Here's hoping that, if Iraola does start the "outstanding" attacker on Wednesday, that he can put on another stellar performance.

#1547. GdS: Strong bonds, Ramos and signings – five reasons for Milan to believe in the Scudetto

AC Milan are five points behind the somewhat surprise league-leaders Lazio, but belief is growing regarding a Scudetto push.

As La Gazzetta dello Sport write, Milan re-emerged from the two-week international break and put in arguably their best performance of the season against Frosinone. They scored five goals and it could have been more, racking up a third league win in a row to move back into the top four.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

The table remains quite tight at the top, with Inter the only team to slip up over the weekend, and the Rossoneri are firmly in the running. The paper highlights give reasons that a title fight is very possible.

Gerry Cardinale and Ruben Amorim are inextricably linked, and that might seem obvious, given that one is the owner and the other the coach. In reality, the bond is deeper than usual, for one simple reason.

Amorim has been handed the keys to create the ‘new Milan’, one that Cardinale has decided to manage completely differently since the end of May. The Portuguese is the coach to whom RedBird have given the longest contract so far, and Cardinale believes he’s the right man at the right time.

He’s demonstrating this concretely not only with his constant presence and his reassuring words, but also with his intention to improve the squad quickly and with the arrival of a key management figure like Markus Krösche. Now, Amorim will receive even greater support.

Gonçalo Inacio, Nicolo Tresoldi, Endrick. These are just some of the names circulating – and these aren’t rumours, but actual targets – ahead of a potentially crucial January transfer window.

The question is obvious: with a couple of top-notch signings for the second half of the season, how far could this team go? Staying up there for starters remains the minimum objective, with Champions League football a must.

Then, Amorim and co. hope that the rest will follow, if their rivals begin to lose pace. The coach is starting to make his team look like they are clicking, but Cardinale has realised the need to accelerate to fill the remaining gaps in the squad.

Amorim (fortunately) quickly realised that the average tactical level of his colleagues in Italy is too high to allow himself to present his Milan team in the same way every single way. So, the 3-4-2-1 that was previously seemingly set in stone has become plasticine in his hands.

The manager moulds and shapes the playing system based on the opponents, rather than his own needs. Since Ruben the fundamentalist became Ruben the quick-change artist, we’ve seen a bit of everything: 4-2-3-1, 4-3-3, 4-4-1-1, 3-5-2.

The former Sporting CP coach coach locks himself in the lab throughout the week and tailors the formation he deems best. Sometimes he gets it wrong, but most of the time he gets it right.

Milan have won five of their last six league games and, game by game, they are increasingly able to camouflage themselves effectively tactically. Opponents never know what formation they will face, while Amorim has several players capable of playing well in multiple roles, which helps.

The data is remarkable and reads as follows: only Rocco (29) and Czeizler (31) coached Milan sides that have scored more goals than Amorim’s (28) in their first 12 Serie A games in charge.

In short, despite all the problems involved (Goncalo Ramos in particular, more on him to come) the coach’s attacking vocation is clearly visible. Furthermore, it is a Milan with a high conversion rate in proportion to the shots on target.

It is also a Diavolo side that have somehow found a way to make up for Ramos’ poor contribution in terms of goals. Alphadjo Cisse, Diego Moreira, Christian Pulisic and Adrien Rabiot take turns to set each other up and score, a sign of a growing offensive physiognomy.

More often than not, a striker simply needs to get a goal in order to build confidence and then begin a virtuous cycle. Milan hope that this is the case for Ramos, who ended his month-long goal drought on Sunday.

However, the reflection goes further: while the Rossoneri having the luxury of being able to score without goals from their No.9 (who is currently on three in the league), surely things can only get better from here?

In short, if the Portuguese international actually does start firing more regularly, then Milan might unlock another dimension to their attack that could really see them surge towards that elusive Scudetto.

#1545. Opinion: Lewis Koumas' future is confirmed, Liverpool's transfer plans confirm it

Lewis Koumas has been a bit of a revelation for Liverpool.

When it was first revealed that Koumas would be staying with the Reds, most people thought he'd be the last option on the Spaniard's list.

However, he's somehow managed to become what looks to be his fourth or fifth-choice attacker.

Granted, most of his playing time has come as a striker but, he can also be used on either wing if needed.

But, with Hugo Ekitike returning and many different attackers now being linked with Liverpool, questions are being asked about what the future has in store for the 21-year-old.

Liverpool have added Gustavo Varela to their shortlist as a long-term target

As mentioned, Koumas has been Isak's back-up so far this season.

The attacker has also been used in other positions but, when Ekitike is back in action, it's hard to see where and how the youngster is going to get a regular role.

That is, unless Ekitike comes back as a fraction of his former self, of course.

Obviously, Liverpool won't want that as they spent around £70 million on the Frenchman last term and, before his injury, he was probably their best player.

So, for Koumas, this season could be his last as a regular first-team option.

That is, especially after the latest transfer update from Football Insider on Liverpool's pursuit of Gustavo Varela.

"Liverpool will not prioritise a move to sign Monza striker Gustavo Varela in January, sources have told Football Insider," they wrote.

Right now, it's unclear exactly what the Reds plan to do with their squad but, the fact that they're already trying to sort their shortlist out for the future means that they must have a pretty accurate idea about what they want to do.

Here's hoping that the Reds sign enough players to make a difference to their team and actually improve it.

They revealed the news on the same day McTominay broke Napoli's three-game losing streak, scoring the winner in a 1-0 victory over Torino.

The procedure took place at the start of September in Manchester, and he was initially supposed to be on the sidelines for two weeks before returning to training.

#1543. Aston Villa news: Why Unai Emery's immunity from criticism should no longer exist

By Darren Plant | 25 Nov 2026 12:36

Such is Unai Emery's status at Aston Villa that few would be surprised if the redeveloped North Stand, when completed in 2027, is named after the Spaniard.

Taking Villa from relegation candidates in 2022-23 to two Champions League qualifications and a Europa League trophy by the conclusion of 2025-26 arguably deserves that level of recognition.

However, despite the expectation that a contract extension past 2029 will be penned in the near future, it will not necessarily strengthen Emery's, or the club's, position in the long term.

Tuesday's 1-0 defeat at Galatasaray extended Villa's recent winless streak across all competitions to six matches. They have failed to score in four of those games, and given up leads on three occasions.

Emery is no stranger to an extended blip in form. At the start of both 2025-26 and 2026-27, Villa were off the pace. It is to Emery's credit that Villa became brief Premier League title contenders in a matter of months and still finished in fourth position in last season's standings.

Nevertheless, Villa are now enduring their second extended winless period of the season, raising the question of whether the West Midlands outfit are experiencing a blip or a gradual decline under their most successful manager for nearly 45 years?

With 116 wins from 215 matches, silverware, and delivering moments and experiences that will last a lifetime, Emery is etched into the Villa history books as a God.

At the same time, this is now a manager of a team that has only recorded 11 wins from his last 27 games in all competitions, as well as losing on 10 occasions. Just seven wins have come from 19 fixtures in 2026-27.

When Villa defeated Tottenham Hotspur, Newcastle United and Manchester City in relatively quick succession with performances that mixed grit, shrewdness and attacking vigour, the conclusion was that Emery's new-looked team had flicked a switch.

However, Villa have regressed as quickly as they had seemingly improved. When you take into account that Villa had one win in seven between February 1 and March 4, and lost three in a row between April 25 and May 3, this is now the fourth "blip" in less than nine months.

Some of the aforementioned statistics will be comparable with managers at similarly-sized clubs in the Premier League and Europe, yet that usually leads to scrutiny over the job that has been conducted over a specific period. Not talk of a contract until 2030 and beyond being signed.

By modern-day standards, Emery is in the unique position of having high control over which players are signed and sold. He essentially has the keys to the footballing side of the club and Villa's fate on the pitch is solely in his hands.

Yet, a 12-time trophy-winning manager of a team that has only earned fewer Premier League points than Arsenal, Manchester City and Liverpool across a four-year period is frequently telling the media, or anyone who will listen, that Villa should not be competing in the top six, nor for the top-eight positions in the league phase of the Champions League.

Is this an example of Emery trying to reinforce the perception that Villa are underdogs to the so-called Premier League 'big six' because of what is, admittedly, a scandalous PSR scenario, or is it a pre-orchestrated approach to defend his position whenever results do not go Villa's way?

Staying on the subject of things being pre-orchestrated, not enough scrutiny is coming over Villa's and Emery's use of Liverpool's Harvey Elliott and Chelsea's Alejandro Garnacho.

Since the summer of 2025, Villa have included £35m and, allegedly, £43m fees with those clubs to sign the players in question should they achieve a specific appearance threshold. Between them, they have made three starts and 13 substitute outings when spending the majority of the time available for selection.

On Tuesday night, Emery omitted Garnacho - who has accumulated fewer than 100 minutes across seven substitute appearances - from the squad for the Galatasaray match, despite naming one fewer substitute than was permitted. Afterwards, he delivered a frank response over the Argentine's chances of earning future game time.

If Villa do not want to pay vast amounts of money for players, they do not have to. However, are Villa not harming their chances of signing players through similar deals in the future? Why should clubs trust such deals to go through if Emery is choosing not to select such players or is being told not to?

Everything points to Garnacho becoming Elliott 2:0 and the situation deserves some clarity. If an honest assessment cannot be delivered to fans and the media, Emery leaves himself open to persistent questioning and criticism, and it will be warranted.

Of course, the evolving Garnacho saga can change for the better. Excluding Villa's game against Chelsea in December, the winger has seven more chances to feature in 2026.

There can be a rapid upturn in fortunes, too. Villa face Ipswich Town, Everton and Crystal Palace in the Premier League before they welcome Paris Saint-Germain to Villa Park in the Champions League.

However, when Emery is storming down tunnels before the full-time whistle, throwing tantrums in the media and getting increasingly frustrated on the touchline as his team look slow, devoid of ideas and can make 700 passes in a game and not score against a team such as Sunderland, it can be argued that Villa need a change of direction rather than remaining on their current path.

Villa have a deep squad with talent that can earn them success in the future, yet they have too many under-performers or players who may simply be tired even at this stage of the season. Whether that is down to Emery, or too much emphasis being placed on players needing to adapt to the "Emery way" before they earn regular starts, it is open to debate.

Regardless, Villa are currently on a downward trajectory under his leadership, and Emery has questions to answer if he is to remain untouchable at a club that want to hand him a contract extension when they could enter December with just three Premier League wins in 2026-27.

#1541. Opinion: Liverpool's new transfer plans will mark the end for Jurgen Klopp favourite

Liverpool have a lot of work to still do on their squad.

Andoni Iraola took charge of the club just after they delivered an extremely shoddy title defence.

They ended up finishing fifth in the Premier League which resulted in them spending another £150 million on new players.

And, while some of those transfers have worked out, it still feels like one or two, such as Bradley Barcola, still have a lot to live up to.

Obviously, as each season goes on, clubs try to add new players to their ranks and, since Liverpool's Premier League title rivals will be doing this, the Reds need to figure out ways to improve their ranks and get back to their best.

Unfortunately, for some of Liverpool's players, this means that their time at Anfield will need to be brought to an end.

On Monday evening, Anfield Watch revealed that Liverpool are eyeing a move for Abdellah Ouazane.

The 17-year-old is currently plying his trade for Ajax in the Eredivisie and, despite being so young, he's already featured in 20 games for the Dutch outfit this term.

During those games, he's contributed to eight goals across all competitions and he has also been played in an array of positions.

The Moroccan was properly promoted to their first-team squad this term after Mika Godts accepted a move to PSG.

Indeed, Ouazane did feature for Ajax once in their domestic cup last season but, this term is the first where he's been a regular part of Miguel Ángel Sánchez Muñoz's team.

To make the deal even sweeter and even more likely, Ouazane is actually a Liverpool fan so, if the Reds went in for him, there's very little chance that he'd say no.

Abdellah Ouazane joining Liverpool would confirm Harvey Elliott's exit

Right now, Liverpool don't really have a proper back-up for Florian Wirtz.

The young German has been the Reds' number 10 for most of the season with James McConnell taking over the role in some of Liverpool's cup games.

And, while McConnell has done a decent job, it's clear that the Reds need to start thinking about having a genuine back-up for Wirtz among their ranks.

Harvey Elliott was probably hoping that would be his role this term but, instead, he's been sent out on loan again.

His time with Valencia started off fairly poorly but, now, he's finally starting to find his feet with his main goal for the campaign likely to be get back on the good side of Iraola.

But, unfortunately for the Englishman, who was often one of the first names on Jurgen Klopp's team sheet, these recent links with Ouazane more or less confirm that his future lies away from Anfield.

That is, unless he can become Valencia's best player and start contributing to goals again.

#1540. Venezia vs. Bologna - prediction, team news, lineups

By Seye Omidiora | 25 Nov 2026 12:37

Venezia head into their matchday 13 encounter with in-form Bologna seeking a third league victory in four matches at Stadio Pier Luigi Penzo.

The Europe-chasing visitors sit 11 places above the Veneto-based club in the Serie A table but will be wary of the Winged Lions' recent improvement in front of their supporters.

On the surface, Venezia's decision to replace Giovanni Stroppa with Davide Nicola has made little difference to their results, with the Lagunari sitting bottom of the league.

However, a closer look suggests that the home supporters can expect a battling performance when Bologna travel to Venice on Friday.

Still the only Serie A side yet to draw this term, the promoted outfit have suffered 10 defeats in 12 matches, including four since Nicola's appointment in October.

Nonetheless, all six of their points have come from their last three matches at Stadio Pier Luigi Penzo, where they have beaten Napoli (1-0) and Udinese (2-1) either side of a 2-0 defeat to Inter Milan.

That loss to the defending champions came courtesy of own goals from Matias Moreno and Redouane Halhal in the final 10 minutes, with the bottom-placed side attempting 12 shots to Inter's 16 and creating two clear-cut chances to the Nerazzurri's three.

Although three matches represent a small sample, those recent performances in Venice suggest that the Lagunari are slowly turning the tide at home, giving Bologna reason for caution ahead of Friday's trip.

Raffaele Palladino's Rossoblu know all about upturns in form, having experienced their own resurgence since Domenico Tedesco was dismissed in mid-September following a winless start to the campaign.

A 1-0 defeat to Napoli at the Maradona proved the final straw for the hierarchy in Bologna, with Palladino inheriting a Felsinei side that had collected just one point from an available 12 across four matches.

Sitting 16th at the time and outside the bottom three only on goal difference, the Rossoblu have since collected 17 points from a possible 24 under Palladino to climb to ninth on 18 points, just three behind sixth-placed Juventus.

Only Lazio (22), AC Milan (19) and Roma (18) have earned more points during that period, underlining Bologna's resurgence since Tedesco's departure as they target a sixth victory in nine league matches.

The travelling supporters will therefore back their in-form side to overcome Nicola's men, although the result may be less straightforward than some anticipate given the Lagunari's steady improvement on home turf.

Toma Basic (muscle), Thierry Correia (thigh), Pasquale Mazzocchi (muscle), Andrea Adorante (hernia), Marin Sverko (hip) and Bartol Franjic (shoulder) are all considered unlikely to feature in gameweek 13.

No player has scored more than twice for the division's lowest scorers, with Akor Adams and Antoine Hainaut netting two apiece to account for half of the Winged Lions' eight league goals.

While Bologna have no individual producing spectacular numbers, they boast a broader spread of match-winners, with Federico Bernardeschi, Samuel Mbangula, Riccardo Orsolini and Tommaso Pobega all scoring twice.

Although Juan Miranda, Nicolo Cambiaghi and Jens Odgaard have yet to score, their respective returns of five, three and two assists underline their importance to the Rossoblu.

However, Bologna must manage without Miranda, who is sidelined alongside Jay Enem (Achilles), Oussama El Azzouzi (thigh) and Emil Holm (thigh).

Stankovic; Halhal, Moreno, Juan Jesus; Hainaut, Kike Perez, Sohm, Busio, Haps; Lauberbach, Adams

Skorupski; Darmian, Casale, Theate; Zortea, Ferguson, Pobega, Cambiaghi; Bernardeschi, Orsolini; Odgaard

Venezia's victories over Napoli and Udinese suggest that their lowly position does not tell the whole story, particularly after they made Inter work for their points in Venice.

However, Bologna's 17-point return from eight matches under Palladino reflects a more sustained improvement, and the visitors should have enough attacking variety to edge Friday's encounter.

#1539. Luke McCowan's timely return to form silences Parkhead critics and boosts midfield options

By JOHN MCGARRY, SCOTTISH CHIEF SPORTS FEATURE WRITER

Published: 11:58 EST, 22 November 2026 | Updated: 12:18 EST, 22 November 2026

Almost everyone who has played the game of football at a professional level has experienced a day where they simply can’t do right for doing wrong.

When one heavy touch leads to another and each decision made seems worse than the last one.

Like the buses in his native Greenock, it was Luke McCowan’s misfortune for two such traumatic experiences to arrive in close proximity.

His inept performance as a substitute on a dark night for Celtic in Linz in August will flash through his mind when he’s old and grey.

Handed the opportunity to atone for it with a start in the league game against Rangers at Parkhead the following month, his withdrawal at half-time felt like an act of mercy.

A Celtic supporter all his days, McCowan didn’t have to speak to articulate the depth of his despair in that trying time. Subjected to a barrage of online criticism, the deletion of his social media accounts said enough.

Luke McCowan scored in the 4-1 home victory over St Mirren

Skipper Callum McGregor and McCowan enjoy the victory at full-time

While you could understand why the midfielder would have felt personally responsible for a pair of high-profile losses, there was a lot more to the team’s shortcomings on those occasions than one man performing as if his laces were tied together.

Away to LASK, Celtic were already wilting when he shed his tracksuit. He didn’t stop the slide towards an extraordinary exit from the Champions League but he didn’t instigate it.

At home to Rangers, Celtic were flat and second-best from the outset and remained that way even after McCowan came inside for the second period.

The 28-year-old was not alone in failing to do himself justice on those occasions and in other matches around what was a difficult period for Martin O’Neill’s side. It might just have felt like it.

As shown by his contributions to a side who were capable of winning the title in his first two seasons in Glasgow, McCowan was – and is – a far more accomplished player than those unfortunate episodes suggested.

He wasn’t the first and he won’t be the last player to suffer a crisis of confidence. And despite being no shrinking violet, he would not be human if those experiences didn’t shake him up and lead him to question if he was worthy of wearing the jersey that he always dreamed of.

His display on Saturday should have emphatically answered those inner doubts.

Trusted by his manager to fill the void created by the injury to Mika Baur, McCowan delivered.

Even before he scored to put the game to bed just before half-time, he played smart passes, made intelligent runs and made key interceptions. He looked very much a Celtic player again.

McGregor takes the acclaim from team-mates after scoring Celtic's fourth goal

No one in O’Neill’s side, in fact, did more to ensure that they went up the tunnel at the interval to warm applause.

With Baur’s absence for up to ten weeks already a source of stress to the Celtic manager, Benjamin Nygren’s sore heel would have further disrupted his sleep on Friday night.

Saturday proved to be quite the day for O’Neill’s fringe men, though.

On top of McCowan’s assured display, we witnessed Alex Oxlade-Chamberlain serve up a reminder of why he once wore the jerseys of Arsenal, Liverpool and England.

Playing deeper than McCowan, Oxlade-Chamberlain stretched St Mirren with his pinpoint passing, long and short. He kept the ball in tight areas and made it all look so simple.

He was in the right place at the right time to stroke home Yang Hyun-jun’s cut-back to put his side in front and never put a foot wrong until his legs could give no more.

The cherry on the cake for O’Neill came by way of Joel van den Berg’s debut from the bench.

Having seen the club shell out over £3million to PSV Eindhoven, Celtic supporters were growing a little concerned that the teenager hadn’t yet featured for the first team.

Now fully recovered from an injury, he belatedly caught the eye. Tall, skilful and rangy, he looked the part. Might he have earned himself a call-up to the Europa League squad as a replacement for Baur? You would not be surprised.

Celtic will certainly travel to Portugal to face Torreense on Thursday in optimistic mood after making short work of seeing off the Buddies.

Arriving just before McCowan turned home Kieran Tierney’s cross, Camilo Duran claimed his 14th of the season by bundling in a brilliant assist from the same source. Stationed on the bench throughout, Kasper Hogh wasn’t even afforded a chance to end his 16-game goal drought.

On a good day for a makeshift midfield, Callum McGregor, its mainstay, claimed Celtic’s fourth with a controlled strike after the break.

Sam Johnstone didn’t have a great deal to do, testament to Celtic’s work without the ball. Tierney was excellent for 71 minutes, despite playing the entirety of Scotland’s games with North Macedonia and Switzerland.

The directness and industry of Yang on the right flank was also eye-catching. Omitted from the squad for the second successive match, Haissem Hassan will surely have taken note.

On the other flank, Jota looked like a player who’s threatening to really fire again.

A late run-out for Auston Trusty, the first since the death of his father, was met by warm applause by home fans. O’Neill will certainly need the American in the coming weeks.

While Killian Phillips did spoil Johnstone’s clean sheet by converting a penalty which the keeper gave away, O’Neill would have had few complaints about a display which saw his side create an abundance of opportunities.

It must be said that St Mirren were their own worst enemies. They are proving to be a strange fish under Craig McLeish. Even in defeat, some of their football on Saturday was eye-catching.

Yet again, though, they showed themselves to be a soft touch defensively. They were fortunate not to ship more than four and it’s hardly a new thing, either.

The Buddies haven’t kept a clean sheet since winning by a goal at Rugby Park on September 2. In the ten subsequent matches, they’ve picked the ball out of their net 23 times. It’s becoming a real concern.

While they are more creative and entertaining than when Stephen Robinson was in charge, they could badly do with becoming as hard to beat as they were under their former boss.

They are now just five points above Kilmarnock ahead of their meeting in Paisley this weekend. That would be an opportune moment for it all to come together.

#1536. Levante vs Racing de Santander - prediction, team news, lineups

By Matt Law | 25 Nov 2026 12:48, Last updated: 25 Nov 2026 12:50

Racing de Santander will be bidding to continue their excellent run of form when they head to Estadi Ciutat de Valencia on Friday evening to tackle Levante.

Levante just about lead the overall head-to-head record between these two sides, winning 11 of their 30 meetings in all competitions, suffering 10 defeats in the process.

Levante have a record of two wins, six draws and five defeats from their 13 league matches this season, with 12 points leaving them down in 15th spot in the La Liga table.

The Frogs have been an entertaining watch at home this season, scoring 14 times and conceding 13, boasting a record of two wins, two draws and two defeats.

Luis Castro's side will enter this match off the back of a 1-1 draw with Elche, while they also drew 0-0 with Celta Vigo before the November international break, with their last victory coming at home to Athletic Bilbao on October 21.

Levante finished 16th in Spain's top flight last season, so there is clear room for improvement in 2026-27, but they have found it difficult to win matches so far this term.

The Frogs actually beat Racing 3-1 in the last match between the two teams in April 2025, but two of their last four meetings have been won by the latter.

Racing, who are the reigning Segunda Division champions, have been one of the stories of the season in Spain's top flight, impressing hugely on their return to La Liga.

The Green and Whites boast a record of five wins, two draws and six defeats from their 13 league matches, which has left them seventh in the table on 17 points.

Jose Alberto's side have actually conceded 32 times in La Liga this season, which is comfortably the worst record in the division, but they have found the back of the net on 20 occasions - the sixth-best attacking record at this stage.

Racing will enter this match off the back of a 3-2 win over Real Sociedad, and they have now been victorious in three of their last four in the league, and four of their last five in all competitions.

The Green and Whites have struggled away from home this season, though, losing five of their six league matches, only managing to pick up three points.

Racing de Santander form (all competitions):

Levante lost Jeremy Toljan to an injury in the early stages of their clash with Elche last time out, and the defender is set to miss out on Friday.

The hosts have not reported any further problems, so aside from Nacho Perez coming in for Toljan at right-back, it could be the same side that started the team's last game.

Roger Brugue has scored five times and registered one assist in 13 appearances this season, and the 30-year-old is again set for a spot in the starting side.

Karl Etta Eyong, though, is likely to start on the bench.

As for Racing, Maguette Gueye, Alvaro Mantilla and Andres Martin could potentially miss the match through injury, but the visitors are otherwise in strong shape.

Yassir Zabiri, who is on loan at the club from Rennes, has been in excellent form this season, scoring 11 times in 13 league appearances, and he will again feature in the final third of the field.

There should also be another spot in the first XI for the experienced Sergio Canales, who has been a key player for the club this term at the age of 35, coming up with two goals and one assist in 13 appearances.

Published: 12:40 EST, 22 November 2026 | Updated: 12:40 EST, 22 November 2026

Tuur Rommens has urged his Rangers team-mates to use a breakneck run of three home games in eight days to build a platform from which to launch a real assault on the Premiership title.

Derek McInnes’ side play host to Aberdeen on Tuesday and then have Falkirk and Dundee United visiting – with Belgian left-back Rommens clear on the need to use the Ibrox atmosphere as a weapon.

‘At the away games, there’s a lot of fans, but at home there’s even more, so it gives an extra boost,’ he said.

‘I think, at home, we have to maintain our good run.

‘We’ll try to keep on winning these three games and then we’ll see from there. If you keep winning, you’ll be up there.

Tuur Rommens (right) celebrates with match-winner Ryan Naderi at Fir Park

Emmanuel Fernandez headed home the opener in Rangers' 2-1 victory at Motherwell

‘I guess Aberdeen, it’s a difficult one, but we’ll try to keep on winning.’

Rommens believes the side’s ability to pull wins out of the fire and show they are willing to keep pushing right to the end of matches is helping build unity within the squad and with their followers.

‘Yeah, exactly,’ he said. ‘Also with the fans, when you score you feel a lot of emotions. You feel that they’re so happy, we’re so happy, so it gives us extra boost to go on Tuesday again and try to get a win.

#1534. Next Lincoln City manager: Chris Cohen, Tom Shaw sacked by Championship club

By Darren Plant | 25 Nov 2026 12:59, Last updated: 25 Nov 2026 12:59

Lincoln City have sacked co-managers Chris Cohen and Tom Shaw.

The pair were promoted from the club's backroom staff after head coach Michael Skubala made the decision to leave the League One champions for Bristol City in the summer.

With Lincoln sitting in 21st place in the Championship table and two points above the relegation zone, a positive spin can be put on the club's first campaign in the second tier of English football for more than 60 years.

However, Tuesday's 4-0 defeat at Charlton Athletic was Lincoln's fifth successive loss in the Championship.

As well as one win and eight defeats being posted across a 10-match period, the club's hierarchy have decided for a change in direction.

A statement read: "We have worked incredibly hard to reach the Championship and will do everything in our power to retain our status in this division.”   "We know how much this football club means to our supporters and are humbled by the level of support we’ve had home and away so far this season."

ℹ️ City can confirm Chris Cohen and Tom Shaw have been relieved of their duties as head coaches with immediate effect. We thank them for their contributions to the club over the last several years and wish them well for the future. https://t.co/mwLolWdxhp

Lincoln add that they will next provide an update on their search for a successor to Cohen and Shaw on November 30.

Despite 15 points coming from 17 matches, Cohen and Shaw can have no complaints over Lincoln's decision.

With Preston North End and Burnley - in 22nd and 23rd position - closing the gap, Lincoln's owners are justified in the move that they have taken.

Furthermore, second-placed Wolverhampton Wanderers are the next visitors to the ProAmpac Stadium on Saturday afternoon.

Likely viewing that game as a free-hit under first-team coach Stuart Pearson, Lincoln will look to have a permanent manager in place for the trip to Cardiff City on December 5.

#1533. Opinion: Liverpool find surprise solution to midfield problems

Liverpool's midfield has been a major topic of conversation for a while now.

Ever since Fabinho left in 2023, fans have demanded that new players were brought in by the Anfield outfit.

Obviously, that still hasn't happened with Arne Slot and Andoni Iraola actually making Liverpool's midfield weaker thanks to their sales of Tyler Morton and Curtis Jones over the last couple of seasons.

In the summer, most fans thought that at least one midfielder would be brought in to replace Jones but, instead, Trey Nyoni was given a more prominent role.

And, while he's done well this term, since he's still so young, he can't be playing two 90 minute games every week which is why a new midfielder now needs to be brought in.

Gavi could be Liverpool's surprise solution to their problems

Over the last few years, many different players have been discussed as potential options for Liverpool to explore.

Recently, Lamine Camara, Adam Wharton and Alex Scott have been the most linked with an Anfield switch.

However, in the upcoming January transfer window, each of them will only be available for crazy high fees.

And, with how many clubs have shown an interest in acquiring their services, there's going to be a huge battle for every single player.

That's why this latest update from journalist Juan Jesus is exciting.

"In addition to Alejandro Balde, Barça are now pushing Gavi out this very winter to fund the signing of a centre-back, seen as the club’s absolute priority," he wrote.

"The main target to bolster the defence is Nico Schlotterbeck, but the current wage bill leaves no room to pull off a move of that magnitude in January.

"To comply with financial fair play rules and try to sign him in this winter window, the board is pushing for two key sales: Balde on one hand, and the bombshell departure of Gavi on the other."

At the start of the 2026-27 season, nobody thought that Gavi would become available on the market.

He's been a regular feature in Flick's plans for as long as anyone can remember and, since he's only 22 years old, there's so much of his career left to go.

Obviously, a deal wouldn't come cheap for the Spaniard but, if the La Liga giants are as strapped for cash as they seem to be, an agreement could probably be reached.

Gavi can also play as a number 10, eight or six which is massively beneficial for the Reds.

This versatility coupled with his endless experience of the Champions League and La Liga all join together to make him the perfect player for Liverpool to sign.

Here's hoping that an agreement can be reached.

#1532. GdS: Why Cisse’s position remains a dilemma despite continuous flow of goals

Alphadjo Cisse is one goal away from double figures for the season, and we have not even reached the end of November yet.

As La Gazzetta dello Sport write, the numbers that Cisse is putting up are those of a centre-forward. He has six goals in 10 Serie A appearances, at an average of one every 74 minutes. In the Europa League he has three (a hat-trick against RB Salzburg), at one every 84 minutes.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

Yet, his role remains a bit of a mystery. Cisse has his own idea of ​​his preferred position on the pitch, even if he’s a bit vague. Speaking after the match against Frosinone, he hinted that he’d like to move into the attacking midfielder position behind the striker.

“I’d have more fun and entertain the fans. It would also be easier to provide assists for my team-mates, something I enjoy and haven’t yet managed to do at AC Milan,” he confessed to Sky.

In Verona’s youth team, where Cisse first emerged, head coach Paolo Sammarco deployed him as a left-sided attacking midfielder. It was a position in which the then 17-year-old then went on to score 16 league goals in a breakout season.

At Catanzaro, in his first professional stint in Serie B under Alberto Aquilani, the Italian played more or less the same role in a 3-4-2-1 system, sometimes a bit wider. Before the serious injury that caused him to miss the final six months of last season, he has scored six goals in 22 games.

Ruben Amorim initially deployed him as a left-sided winger, also due to Christian Pulisic’s temporary unavailability. He would later move him further forward and more centrally, to take up the spaces a striker would, a position he has played for Italy U21s under Silvio Baldini.

In this position, Cisse can utilise his extraordinary ability to position himself between the ball and the defender, before turning, aiming and often finishing first time. Despite not being physically big (at 180cm tall), he is strong and has a low centre of gravity that makes him tough to bump off the ball.

⚽️ GOAL ALPHADJO CISSE! 🔥 https://t.co/aMIgE9PXHc

— SempreMilan (@SempreMilanCom) November 22, 2026

This is where the dilemma arises. At Verona and Catanzaro, Alphadjo Cisse impressed because of his speed and agility. After the injury and under the watch of Amorim, he has become more of a positioning-based player, barely ever tearing down the flank.

So far this season, he’s attempted only 16 dribbles at just over three per game, and has only succeeded on five. With one successful dribble per game on average, his success rate is just over 31% (FotMob data).

These numbers perhaps help explain Cisse’s progression close to the penalty area, and also a concept that the player himself has repeated in recent months regarding where he is at in his personal development. On Sunday, he declared: “I’m not even halfway to my potential.”

Who knows if Alpha is referring to his overall growth, with horizons still unexplored, or perhaps his post-injury recovery. Amorim will continue to ponder things, but this is far from a headache, because the rule seems to be well established: if Cisse plays, he tends to score.
